picks.blurb: The Kennesaw State Owls (1-4, 0-1 CUSA) won this league last year and were expected to contend for the title again, but they've had a disappointing start to the year and have dropped back-to-back one-score games. Most recently, they lost 27-26 to Jacksonville State in their league opener. The Missouri State Bears (1-4, 0-1 CUSA), meanwhile, were a surprising bowl team last year in their first season at the FBS level. However, with a new coaching staff this season, they've struggled and are still looking for their first FBS win. He has help behind him too. Plaster Stadium TV: CBS Sports Network | Watch Live RADIO: KSU Owl Network | Listen: KSU Owls App, Tune In | Online: KSUOwls.com | Satellite: SiriusXM 261 Team Info: Game Notes/Depth Charts | Clippings | 2026 Football Media Guide • Kennesaw State football looks to get back on track and even its Conference USA record when it heads to Springfield, Missouri for the second time in program history to take on Missouri State on Wednesday, Oct. 14 at Robert W. Plaster Stadium. • The Owls are coming off back-to-back heartbreaking one-score losses, falling 17-14 to Arkansas State and 27-26 to Jax State. The Bears have lost three-straight entering Wednesday, including a 34-13 defeat to WKU last week. • In its CUSA opener last week, Kennesaw State looked as good as it has offensively all season, recording the eighth-most FBS offensive yards in program history (411) and seventh-most passing yards (293) in a single game. • After averaging just 87 rushing yards against Georgia State and Tennessee, the Owls have found another gear, averaging 157 yards per game over their last two weeks. • Through five games, Kennesaw State ranks fourth in CUSA in points allowed (23.4), but has allowed just 18.8 points per game against non-Power 4 opponents. • Kennesaw State is the only CUSA team with four players who have rushed for at least 100 yards and a score in 2026 and one of only 20 teams in FBS. • Kennesaw State has scored at least 24 points in nine-straight regular-season conference games. • Sr. WR Brayden Munroe recorded the second-most receiving yards in program history last week against Jax State, hauling in seven catches for 159 yards -- second-most of any receiver in CUSA this season. • Munroe leads the team with 299 receiving yards on 19 catches, ranking sixth in the league with 59.8 receiving yards per game. • r-So. LB Tywon Christopher had a career night as well last week, recording 15 tackles, 2.0 tackles for loss and a forced fumble. He is one of only two players in FBS this season to record those numbers in a single game. • Kennesaw State has created havoc for teams this season, ranking second in the conference with seven turnovers gained (five fumble recoveries and two interceptions), and ranking 10th nationally (first in CUSA) with the five fumble recoveries. Single-game tickets begin for as low as $25. Catch all the action of Kennesaw State’s Conference USA schedule that includes matchups against Liberty (Oct. 22), Delaware (Nov. 7) and FIU (Nov. 21). LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Brad Crawford and Chris Hummer are back with their weekly picks and predictions for the weekend's best games Getty Images The Week 7 schedule features six top-25 matchups, giving contenders ample opportunity to strengthen their playoff cases before next month's first selection committee rankings . Nearing the midway point, preseason expectations now carry little weight -- ask teams like LSU, Texas &M, Michigan and Penn State -- with narratives already materializing. We're picking several of Saturday's showdowns that come with playoff implications, raising the stakes for teams in the SEC, Big Ten and Big 12 trying to protect unbeaten records . Ohio State-Indiana, Notre Dame-BYU, Alabama-Tennessee -- good luck finding a quiet window on this slate. Season results : Brad Crawford (38-13 straight up, 29-21-1 ATS); Chris Hummer (40-11 straight up, 27–23-1 ATS) We're coming off my personal worst picks week of my career straight up (3-5, yuck!) after a bevy of upsets I didn't see coming. The against-the-spread total wasn't fatal, at least. Hummer has narrowed the gap to two games back ATS and has assumed the lead straight up after a terrific showing. If these picks aren't enough this week, head to our CBS Sports expert picks page where Hummer's on a heater. No. 16 Mississippi State at No. 22 LSU (-10.5) Hummer ( LSU -10.5) : This game sets up for a LSU bounce back. Even if Kamario Taylor were healthy -- and his status is in doubt this week -- the Tigers have a lot of advantages in this game, including an elite secondary and pass rush. The big question for LSU is whether Sam Leavitt can avoid turnovers. If he plays clean, which has been a problem all year given that he leads the nation in INTs, LSU should roll. … LSU 38, Mississippi State 24. Crawford (LSU -10.5) : Is this the week LSU finally puts it together against an opponent of substance? It is time the Tigers look the part as a potential CFP team after two SEC losses already. A third ends any hope of getting to the 12-team bracket, even if LSU wins out from there and finishes 9-3. The resume simply won't be good enough to warrant enough attention. I'm giving this the must-win label for Lane Kiffin, whose first season is teetering on total disappointment if he's handed a third loss before playing Alabama in November. ... LSU 37, Mississippi State 20. Florida at No. 7 Texas (-9.5) Hummer ( Florida +9.5) : Which version of Arch Manning and the Texas passing attack are we going to get? That's going to determine whether Texas rolls in this game. The Gators have the worst pass defense in the SEC and have been torched by far less talented (on paper) passing attacks than Texas. But Texas has been incredibly inconsistent on offense this year, ranking just 62nd nationally in passing yards per game. Texas, a top-15 rushing defense, is set up to contain Jadan Baugh and Florida's rushing attack. But can it score enough to cover in this one? I'm extremely skeptical. Perhaps Texas responds and blows Florida out -- a real possibility -- but that's just not the team we've seen this year. … Texas 31, Florida 24. Crawford (Texas -9.5) : I'm not positive on this, but the public play will assuredly be Florida, given the potential hangover effect from the Longhorns' loss to Oklahoma . The Gators stink worse, though, with consecutive blowout losses in SEC play since starting the season 4-0 and ranked No. 8. Florida's secondary looks atrocious after being carved up by LaNorris Sellers last week and Arch Manning could do the same. Manning has been off more than sharp this fall, but this is a matchup I like for the Texas offense. The Longhorns lost to Florida last season, and that could play a role in Saturday's performance, too. ... Texas 34, Florida 24. No. 6 Alabama (-6.5) at No. 14 Tennessee Hummer (Alabama -6.5) : The Vols have survived this year behind an elite defense. That unit has carried an offense that ranks just 66th nationally in yards per play and 110th in passing yards per game. But is that defense good enough to hold off Alabama? I'm highly skeptical. Alabama's defense has been susceptible in the secondary this year. But the Vols don't have the passing offense to take advantage of that. The Crimson Tide roll in this game for a second straight year. … Alabama 24, Tennessee 17. Crawford (Alabama -6.5) : It almost feels disrespectful to call this a "get-right" game for the Crimson Tide given their recent struggles at Neyland Stadium, but unless DeSean Bishop controls this game on the ground for the Vols, I don't see a path to a Tennessee victory. The passing game is a struggle for Josh Heupel, and Alabama can score points in a hurry. Falling behind in the first half could lead to a chorus of boos in Knoxville if the Crimson Tide's defense can put together stops. This is a dangerous game for Tennessee, not so much the betting favorites even without Ryan Coleman-Williams on the outside. ... Alabama 30, Tennessee 17. No. 13 Missouri at No. 9 Ole Miss (-6.5) Hummer ( Missouri +6.5) : Ole Miss should have a detailed scouting report on Austin Simmons in this one given that Pete Golding faced him every day for years at Ole Miss. This game will tell us a lot about whether the Rebels' secondary is really any better after their blowout loss to Florida. Missouri is an excellent team. The Tigers are stout up front defensively and have a passing attack that can expose Ole Miss' defense. This game has a ton of star power crossover -- Kewan Lacy went from Missouri to Ole Miss, Simmons from Oxford to Columbia -- and I think it is close throughout. … Ole Miss 31, Missouri 28. Crawford (Missouri +6.5) : Is there anyone out there who saw this being a top-15 matchup a month ago? The Tigers' run without Ahmad Hardy has really been impressive. Jamal Roberts has back-to-back 200-yard outings on the ground and could easily have a third against a defense that's had its issues this season. I like Missouri in this spot with the points. I'm still not sure what to make of the Rebels outside of Trinidad Chambliss . You know what you're getting out of him, but Kewan Lacy is banged up and play on the other side of the football has left much to be desired. ... Ole Miss 30, Missouri 24. No. 18 Oklahoma State at No. 20 Houston (-3.5) Hummer ( Oklahoma State +3.5) : The Cowboys have gotten better every week this season to the point where, with their offense, you can really start to imagine them as an immediate Big 12 title threat. But this is by far their in Big 12 play. Houston is among the nation's best rushing attacks, and Oklahoma State is among the least successful run defenses in the country on a down-to-down basis. Houston plays more zone coverage than any other Big 12 team to prevent big plays. Houston's secondary hasn't succeeded in that area, given the Cougars' rank of 126th nationally in passes allowed of 20-plus yards. This game will come down to two areas: 1. Can Houston control the clock and convert in the red zone? 2. Can Oklahoma State create chunk plays in the passing game? I'm not willing to pick the outright upset here, but I think the Cowboys are in position to have a lot of offensive success in this one. … Houston 31, Oklahoma State 28. Crawford (Oklahoma State +3.5) : Oklahoma State's path to an upset starts with explosive plays while trying to keep Conner Weigman contained on the other side of the football. The Cowboys don't need to dominate every snap if they're turning opportunities into chunk plays and touchdowns. Force Houston to chase points, and suddenly the pressure shifts to the favorite at home in front of what Willie Fritz hopes will be a sellout crowd. This is a matchup with significant Big 12 title game implications, especially since the Cougars already have a loss in conference play at Texas Tech . ... Oklahoma State 34, Houston 31. Penn State at Michigan (-5.5) Hummer (Michigan -5.5) : The losing coach in this one is going to be feeling very uncomfortable. If Penn State falls, it'll be four straight dropped games. If Michigan loses, the Wolverines will have lost three in a row and will be out of the playoff hunt before the calendar turns to November. Michigan will have to run to win in this one. The Nittany Lions have an excellent secondary and, to be kind, Michigan's passing attack has been far from a strength. The good news for the Wolverines is that the Nittany Lions rank 113th nationally in yards allowed per carry. Coming out of a bye -- and given Penn State's struggles to run the football -- I like the Wolverines to cover. … Michigan 27, Penn State 21. Crawford (Penn State +5.5) : Neither of these teams has won a game in the Big Ten, and it's mid-October. That's unacceptable for two first-year staffs at these respective blueblood programs. Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 6:44 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 4 Ohio State travels to No. 5 Indiana for a massive Big Noon showdown. Can the Buckeyes avenge last year's Big Ten Championship loss? One of the biggest games of the college football season is set for Saturday afternoon as No. 4 Ohio State travels to Bloomington to take on No. 5 Indiana in FOX's Big Noon Saturday showdown. And there is plenty of bad blood between these two programs. The last time these teams met, Indiana stunned Ohio State 13-10 in the 2025 Big Ten Championship Game, ending the Buckeyes' undefeated season. Now, Ryan Day and Ohio State have an opportunity to return the favor against Curt Cignetti's defending national champions. Ohio State enters at 5-1, while Indiana remains undefeated at 6-0. Both teams are 3-0 in Big Ten play, making this matchup potentially decisive in the conference championship race. Ohio State: Can Julian Sayin Deliver? Ohio State's offense has been explosive this season, averaging more than 42 points per game. Quarterback Julian Sayin has thrown for approximately 1,772 yards, while superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has been nearly unstoppable, recording 48 receptions for 916 yards and 11 touchdowns. Smith is the most dangerous player in college football, and Indiana's secondary will have its hands full trying to contain him. However, last year's championship game exposed some serious problems for Ohio State. Sayin threw for 258 yards, and Smith recorded eight catches for 144 yards, but the Buckeyes managed just 10 points. Sayin was also sacked five times. Indiana's defensive front remains dangerous, averaging 3.3 sacks and 8.2 tackles for loss per game this season. Running back Bo Jackson, who has rushed for approximately 460 yards, must help establish balance and prevent Indiana from focusing entirely on Sayin. Indiana: The Hoosiers Aren't Going Anywhere Indiana might have lost Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza, but Curt Cignetti has kept the Hoosiers rolling. TCU transfer Josh Hoover has thrown for more than 1,300 yards with 17 touchdowns and zero interceptions, while running back Turbo Richard has rushed for nearly 600 yards. Wide receiver Charlie Becker has also been outstanding, recording 529 receiving yards and eight touchdowns. Michigan State transfer Nick Marsh gives Indiana another dangerous weapon on the outside. Defensively, Indiana is allowing approximately 12 points per game and has demonstrated an ability to create pressure without sacrificing coverage. However, the Hoosiers haven't exactly dominated their recent competition. Indiana narrowly escaped Northwestern 29-23 before defeating Nebraska 20-17 last weekend. Those performances raise questions about whether the Hoosiers can consistently move the football against an elite opponent. Expect another physical, defensive battle between two legitimate College Football Playoff contenders. Indiana's defense will create problems for Sayin, and the Hoosiers should find success moving the football through Hoover and Richard. However, Ohio State has something Indiana doesn't: Jeremiah Smith. I expect Smith to deliver a massive performance, surpassing 100 receiving yards and making the difference in a game that comes down to the final possession. Sayin will make a few mistakes under pressure, but the Buckeyes' defense will get enough stops to escape Bloomington with a huge victory. Final Score: No. 4 Ohio State 24, No. 5 Indiana 20 Ohio State gets its revenge, hands Indiana its first loss of the season, and puts itself in an excellent position in the Big Ten championship race. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Cole VanWiechen Wed, October 14, 2026 at 9:01 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is the one Ohio State fans have had circled since December. No. 4 Ohio State travels to No. 5 Indiana on Saturday at noon ET on FOX for a rematch of last year's 13-10 Big Ten title game loss in Indianapolis. The Buckeyes are 3.5-point favorites, but going into Bloomington against the defending national champions is about as tough a road test as there is in the Big Ten. What to know about Indiana's offense Indiana looks a little different than last year, but they're still very good. The Hoosiers rank 20th nationally at 462.7 yards per game and average 40.2 points per game, also inside the top 20. They're balanced too, averaging 241 passing yards and 221 rushing yards a game. Josh Hoover has been excellent since transferring in from TCU. He's completing about 70% of his passes with 17 touchdowns and zero interceptions. That's a huge change for a quarterback whose biggest knock coming in was that he was interception prone. That says a lot about Curt Cignetti's coaching staff. The backfield is a two-headed monster in Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr., who both have over 550 rushing yards. Richard is averaging 8.4 yards per carry. The receiver room is just as dangerous. Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh both have 30 catches for 530 yards. Becker has eight touchdowns and Marsh has six, and it's hard to find a better receiver duo in the Big Ten. What to know about Indiana's defense The defense might be even better. Indiana is allowing just 11.8 points per game, fifth in the country, and 237.8 yards per game, fourth nationally. The Hoosiers also haven't lost the turnover battle in a single game this season. The pass rush is led by Tobi Osunsami and Stephen Daley, who each have five sacks. Isaiah Jones and Rojiah Hardy are a strong linebacker duo in the middle. This is a complete, well-coached defense that won't give Ohio State much for free. Most important matchups Osunsami and Daley vs. Ohio State's offensive tackles . This might be the biggest matchup of the game. Phillip Daniels' status is still worth watching, and whoever starts at the other tackle spot has to hold up against two edge rushers with five sacks apiece. If Indiana can get to Julian Sayin, it changes everything. Devin Sanchez and Jermaine Mathews Jr. vs. Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh . Ohio State's corners just had their best combined game of the season against Maryland. Becker and Marsh are a completely different level of challenge, and Becker made two of the biggest catches against Mathews in last year's title game. Julian Sayin vs. a good team . Last year against Indiana, Sayin went 21-of-29 for 258 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He was solid, but Ohio State needed more. Sayin is coming off a sloppy game against Maryland, and this is his chance to show he can be the difference in a game like this.

picks.blurb: ESPN FPI Predicts Tight Finish Between Indiana and Ohio State In Top-Five Clash - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NLCS Game 3 updates NFL hot seats Champions League results Heisman Watch ESPN FPI Predicts Tight Finish Between Indiana and Ohio State In Top-Five Clash Oct 10, 2026; Lincoln, Nebraska, USA; Indiana Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti looks on during a timeout against the Nebraska Cornhuskers during the second quarter at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dylan Widger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Zach Browning Mon, October 12, 2026 at 10:44 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Indiana's narrow 20-17 victory over Nebraska kept the Hoosiers undefeated, but ESPN's computers still give Ohio State the slightest of advantages heading into Saturday's top-five showdown at Memorial Stadium. The No. 5 Hoosiers (6-0) welcome the No. 4 Buckeyes (5-1) to Bloomington for a noon kickoff on FOX, with ESPN's Football Power Index projecting a game that could go either way. ESPN FPI gives Ohio State a narrow edge ESPN's latest FPI rankings have Ohio State at No. 3 nationally and Indiana at No. 7, but the gap between the two nearly disappears when accounting for Saturday's matchup in Bloomington. The model gives Ohio State a 52.2% chance of winning, with a projected margin of just 0.7 points. The Buckeyes are also 3.5-point favorites according to Monday's betting lines. ESPN's SP+ model sees an even closer contest, projecting a 26.4-26.2 Ohio State victory and giving the Buckeyes a 51% chance of winning. Essentially, the computers see a toss-up. That's a notable shift from the preseason, when the FPI gave Indiana just a 39.2% chance of defeating Ohio State. The Hoosiers have since improved those odds to 47.8%, reflecting how closely the two teams are viewed entering Saturday. What the projections mean for Indiana Ohio State presents Indiana with its toughest challenge of the season, particularly on offense. The Buckeyes are averaging 42.7 points per game, while quarterback Julian Sayin has thrown 17 touchdowns against just two interceptions. Then there's Jeremiah Smith, who may be college football's best player. But Indiana has its own reasons for confidence. The Hoosiers have won 22 consecutive games, including last December's 13-10 victory over Ohio State in the Big Ten Championship Game. Indiana has also yet to lose at Memorial Stadium under Curt Cignetti. And despite needing a fourth-quarter comeback to escape Nebraska, Indiana has repeatedly demonstrated an ability to win games that don't go according to plan. Indiana's offense struggled to establish its ground game against Nebraska, finishing with just 66 rushing yards on 22 attempts. That's a concerning number heading into a matchup with an Ohio State defense allowing 13.2 points per game. The Hoosiers likely won't be able to afford another similarly one-dimensional offensive performance against the Buckeyes. Still, with the game in Bloomington and both teams among the nation's best, the difference between victory and defeat could come down to a handful of plays. For all the attention surrounding Saturday's showdown, ESPN's projections suggest there may be very little separating Indiana and Ohio State. Pete Fiutak Wed, October 14, 2026 at 6:42 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Just a few weeks ago, Florida was coming off a 52-28 obliteration of a terrific Ole Miss team, and everything was wonderful. The Gators appeared good enough in the first season under Jon Sumrall to be in the SEC and College Football Playoff mix, the offense was unstoppable, and then a funny thing happened. The SEC figured it out. Missouri and South Carolina beat Florida by a combined score of 83-36, and now, with the schedule ahead, the 4-2 team might have to fight just to get to a bowl game. Last week at this time, Texas was No. 1, it was about to play a punchless Oklahoma team, and then a funny thing happened. The Sooners came up with creative and clutch ways to pull off a 27-24 Red River Rivalry win. The season is hardly over for the Longhorns, but now there's little margin for error over a tough second half. Florida vs Texas: Quick Hits It doesn't get any easier for Florida after this, with a week off before dealing with Georgia, followed up by Oklahoma, and then a trip to Kentucky. Texas starts a run of three straight home games, getting Ole Miss next and Mississippi State to follow. How is this only the sixth game between these two? Texas is 3-1-1, with the 7-7 tie coming in the first meeting in 1924. How To Watch Florida vs Texas Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ABC Location: DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin, TX – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Florida Will Win The defense isn't getting fixed over the next few weeks, but that's part of what a rebuild is all about. The Gators win when the offense rocks, and the yards and points allowed are simply the cost of doing business. However, there's one key element to the Florida D that should show up huge. The pass rush is outstanding. The Gator defensive front averages close to three sacks and seven tackles for loss per game, and as good as Arch Manning is – seriously, he's really good, despite the popular opinions at the moment after the OU loss – he's still not amazing when he's getting rushed. The Texas offensive line has been better than last year for the ground game, but the pass protection has been a problem. Why Texas Will Win The Texas defense is going to stuff the Florida offense cold. Missouri and South Carolina never let Gator star Jadan Baugh and the running game breathe. The Gamecocks and Tigers combined for 18 tackles for loss against the Florida attack, and both allowed fewer than 400 yards of total offense. For all the problems in the meltdown against Oklahoma, the Texas defense was great. It allowed only 238 yards of Sooner offense, and for the fourth game in a row – including against Ohio State and Tennessee – the defense allowed fewer than 100 rushing yards. Florida vs Texas Prediction, Betting Lines It turned out to be one of the most important games of the 2025 season. Florida finished the year 4-8, but one of those wins was a 29-21 thriller over Texas. The Longhorns lost on the road to both Ohio State and Georgia – no shame there against two teams that finished with 12 wins – but that loss to the Gators kept them out of the College Football Playoff. Yeah, Texas lost to Oklahoma, but weird things happen in the Red River Rivalry. Against Florida, the offense will keep it conservative, but Arch will connect on a few deep shots to push ahead. The defense will take care of the rest. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:36 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 7 Texas looks to bounce back against Florida after a devastating loss to Oklahoma. Can Arch Manning silence his critics and save the Longhorns' season? No. 7 Texas (4-1) returns home Saturday afternoon to face Florida (4-2) in a massive SEC matchup between two programs desperate for a bounce-back victory. The Longhorns are coming off an embarrassing 27-24 loss to Oklahoma, while Florida was dominated 38-19 at home by South Carolina. Both teams entered the season with championship aspirations, but another loss could seriously damage their College Football Playoff hopes. And for Texas quarterback Arch Manning, the pressure has never been higher. Texas: It's Time for Arch Manning to Deliver Manning entered the season as one of the Heisman Trophy favorites, but his performances have been anything but consistent. Through five games, Manning has thrown for 1,122 yards, 10 touchdowns, and five interceptions. Against Oklahoma, he completed 19 of 31 passes for 260 yards and three touchdowns, but two costly fourth-quarter interceptions helped the Sooners erase a 17-7 halftime deficit. The Longhorns are averaging just 379.2 yards per game, ranking 79th nationally. That's simply unacceptable considering the offensive talent Steve Sarkisian has assembled. However, Saturday presents an excellent opportunity to get things back on track. Florida's defense is allowing 393 yards and 29 points per game, including an alarming 268.7 passing yards per contest. Wide receiver Cam Coleman, who has 318 receiving yards and five touchdowns, should have opportunities to create explosive plays against a struggling Gators secondary. Defensively, Texas has been outstanding, allowing just 16 points and 96 rushing yards per game. Edge rusher Colin Simmons has been nearly unstoppable, recording 9.5 sacks. Florida: Can Jadan Baugh Save the Gators? Florida's offense has actually been impressive this season, averaging 41.7 points and 473.8 yards per game. Quarterback Aaron Philo has thrown for 1,341 yards, nine touchdowns, and three interceptions, while receiver Dallas Wilson has recorded 376 yards and three touchdowns. However, the biggest storyline is running back Jadan Baugh. Baugh has rushed for 672 yards and 12 touchdowns, establishing himself as one of the SEC's most productive backs. Unfortunately, his production has slowed considerably. Over Florida's last two games, Baugh has managed just 72 rushing yards, including 59 yards on 15 carries against South Carolina. That's a major concern considering Texas possesses one of the nation's best rushing defenses. Florida also defeated Texas 29-21 last season, meaning the Gators have already proven they're capable of beating Sarkisian's program. But winning in Austin will be a completely different challenge. How Each Team Wins For Texas, the formula starts with protecting Manning and establishing an early rhythm through the passing game. The Longhorns must take advantage of Florida's vulnerable secondary while allowing their defensive front to disrupt Philo and contain Baugh. For Florida, everything revolves around getting Baugh going early. If the Gators can establish their rushing attack, they'll have opportunities to control possession and keep Manning on the sidelines. Defensively, Florida must force Manning into mistakes, something Oklahoma successfully accomplished last weekend. I expect Texas to respond with a much more disciplined performance following its disappointing loss to Oklahoma. Manning should have opportunities to attack Florida's secondary, but I'm still not convinced he's capable of consistently dominating SEC competition. Expect a solid, rather than spectacular, performance from the Texas quarterback. The biggest difference will be Texas' defense. With Simmons creating pressure and the Longhorns limiting Baugh's rushing opportunities, Florida will struggle to sustain drives throughout the afternoon. I expect the Gators to keep things competitive early, but Texas will gradually take control in the second half. Final Score: No. 7 Texas 27, Florida 17 Texas gets back in the win column, improves to 5-1, and keeps its College Football Playoff hopes alive. The Florida Gators can put the Texas Longhorns' College Football Playoff hopes on life support this weekend in Austin. Both teams are looking to rebound from losses last weekend. Texas suffered its first loss of the season last Saturday, falling 27-24 to Oklahoma. Florida, meanwhile, has now lost two games after getting upset at home in a 38-19 loss to South Carolina. If Texas loses this weekend, they'll likely need to win out to make the 12-team playoff. ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Florida vs Texas ESPN's Greg McElroy made his score predictions for this weekend's biggest games, and he has Texas beating Florida 31-17. "Where does Florida find 21 points?" said McElroy. "Florida scored 17 and 19 in their last two games against SEC defenses. When this (Texas) team allows fewer than 21 points, Steve Sarkisian is 63-4 as an FBS head coach. Now, Florida's best route there is the short field off of a Texas mistake because this Texas defense, they almost never let long drives finish in the end zone. "I'm taking Texas to win the game 31-17. I think Texas will win on third down all afternoon, because Florida's defense is probably going to have a hard time getting off the field, and I think Texas is built to live in short yardage. Florida's offense has stalled the last couple of weeks against SEC defenses, and this is the best defense I think they've seen so far. And that's no disrespect to South Carolina or Missouri — Texas is a step up in competition and personnel. … So we think Texas wins this game by a couple of touchdowns, but I do think both defenses will play well enough to keep it relatively low scoring. Texas wins this one slowly and on schedule. Whether or not we see the offensive fireworks is one of the biggest questions in the game." Can Lane Kiffin and the Tigers bounce back after an embarrassing loss? The pressure is mounting in Baton Rouge as No. 22 LSU (4-2) prepares to host No. 16 Mississippi State (4-2) Saturday afternoon at Tiger Stadium. Lane Kiffin's Tigers are coming off an embarrassing 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky, a game LSU had every opportunity to win before a questionable fourth-down decision allowed the Wildcats to force overtime. Meanwhile, Mississippi State is looking to bounce back after a disappointing loss to Alabama. With LSU already sitting at 1-2 in SEC play, another conference loss could effectively end the Tigers' College Football Playoff hopes. LSU: Can Sam Leavitt Save the Tigers? LSU's offense has shown flashes of brilliance under Kiffin, but consistency remains a major concern. Quarterback Sam Leavitt has thrown for 1,495 yards and 10 touchdowns, but his eight interceptions are the most of any quarterback in the SEC. Those turnovers have been a major issue for a team that possesses enough offensive talent to compete with nearly anyone. Running back Dilin Jones has provided stability in the backfield, rushing for 426 yards and five touchdowns through LSU's first five games. Wide receiver Winston Watkins Jr. has also emerged as a dangerous weapon, recording 354 receiving yards. Defensively, LSU has been impressive at times, particularly with edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, who recorded eight sacks through the team's first five games. However, the Tigers just surrendered 35 points to Kentucky, raising serious questions about their ability to close out games. Against Mississippi State's explosive offense, LSU cannot afford another inconsistent defensive performance. Mississippi State: Kamario Taylor Is a PROBLEM Jeff Lebby has Mississippi State playing some exciting football, and quarterback Kamario Taylor has emerged as one of the SEC's most dangerous young players. Taylor has thrown for 1,450 yards, 17 touchdowns, and just four interceptions while completing 66.2% of his passes. However, his availability is a major concern after aggravating a lower-leg injury against Alabama. If Taylor is healthy enough to play, LSU's defense will have its hands full. Wide receiver Anthony Evans III has been outstanding, recording 40 receptions for 574 yards and five touchdowns through five games. Running back Fluff Bothwell has also been productive, rushing for 403 yards and three touchdowns while averaging 5.4 yards per carry. The Bulldogs possess enough offensive firepower to challenge LSU, but their defense remains vulnerable. Mississippi State was allowing 28 points and nearly 380 yards per game through its first five contests. That's a dangerous weakness against a Kiffin-led offense playing at home. How Each Team Wins For LSU, everything starts with protecting the football. Leavitt must avoid costly interceptions and take advantage of Mississippi State's vulnerable secondary. Establishing Jones early should also create opportunities for explosive passing plays. Defensively, LSU needs to pressure Taylor if he plays and prevent Evans from creating big plays downfield. For Mississippi State, the formula revolves around attacking LSU's defense with tempo and forcing Leavitt into mistakes. If Taylor is available, his dual-threat ability could create serious problems. The Bulldogs must also establish Bothwell to prevent LSU from focusing entirely on the passing game. I expect an offensive shootout in Baton Rouge. Mississippi State has enough offensive talent to create problems for LSU, particularly if Taylor is healthy enough to play. However, I believe this is a bounce-back opportunity for Kiffin and the Tigers. Leavitt should have success attacking Mississippi State's secondary, and I expect him to throw for more than 300 yards and three touchdowns. The Bulldogs will keep things competitive throughout the afternoon, but LSU's home-field advantage and offensive firepower should ultimately make the difference. Expect Mississippi State to threaten late before LSU's defense comes up with a crucial stop to secure the victory. Final Score: No. 22 LSU 38, No. 16 Mississippi State 31 LSU survives a major scare, improves to 5-2, and keeps its College Football Playoff hopes alive. away.blurb: An unheralded and unranked recruit out of high school in the 2025 signing class, Puckett seems to have won the backup job behind Taylor, but what would coach Jeff Lebby do with a full week to prepare for a game without his star quarterback? No. 16 Mississippi State may have to face No. 22 LSU in Death Valley without its star quarterback. CBS Sports' John Talty has confirmed that Taylor's status for the game is uncertain due to a foot injury, which was first reported by ESPN . Toward the end of Mississippi State's 56-23 loss to Alabama , Taylor was seen dealing with an injury on the sideline. It seems that the issue has lingered through the open date and could keep Taylor from playing against LSU. Taylor has taken a big step forward this fall, and he is the main reason behind the Bulldogs' 4-1 start to the season. The sophomore quarterback has completed 66.2% of his passes for 1,450 yards and leads the SEC with 17 touchdown passes. On top of that, Taylor has used his legs to pick up 159 yards and a touchdown on the ground. Prior to the Bulldogs' loss to Alabama, Taylor had thrust himself into the Heisman Trophy conversation. Even in that losing effort, Taylor made some big plays, although his three turnovers proved to be costly. If Taylor can't go against the Tigers, an already daunting task gets even tougher for Mississippi State. When Taylor left the Alabama game, Parker Puckett was the first quarterback off the bench in relief. Former Appalachian State quarterback AJ Swann, a senior, is far and away the most experienced player in that position room with 24 career games under his belt. Jaden Rashada, a former top-50 recruit, is also on the roster and could provide the offense with some degree of upside.

home.blurb: An unheralded and unranked recruit out of high school in the 2025 signing class, Puckett seems to have won the backup job behind Taylor, but what would coach Jeff Lebby do with a full week to prepare for a game without his star quarterback? No. 16 Mississippi State may have to face No. 22 LSU in Death Valley without its star quarterback. CBS Sports' John Talty has confirmed that Taylor's status for the game is uncertain due to a foot injury, which was first reported by ESPN . Toward the end of Mississippi State's 56-23 loss to Alabama , Taylor was seen dealing with an injury on the sideline. It seems that the issue has lingered through the open date and could keep Taylor from playing against LSU. Taylor has taken a big step forward this fall, and he is the main reason behind the Bulldogs' 4-1 start to the season. The sophomore quarterback has completed 66.2% of his passes for 1,450 yards and leads the SEC with 17 touchdown passes. On top of that, Taylor has used his legs to pick up 159 yards and a touchdown on the ground. Prior to the Bulldogs' loss to Alabama, Taylor had thrust himself into the Heisman Trophy conversation. Even in that losing effort, Taylor made some big plays, although his three turnovers proved to be costly. If Taylor can't go against the Tigers, an already daunting task gets even tougher for Mississippi State. When Taylor left the Alabama game, Parker Puckett was the first quarterback off the bench in relief. Former Appalachian State quarterback AJ Swann, a senior, is far and away the most experienced player in that position room with 24 career games under his belt. Jaden Rashada, a former top-50 recruit, is also on the roster and could provide the offense with some degree of upside.

Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 1 Georgia hosts Auburn in the Deep South's Oldest Rivalry. After dominating Alabama physically, the Bulldogs could embarrass the Tigers. The Deep South's Oldest Rivalry returns to Athens this Saturday as No. 1 Georgia (6-0) welcomes Auburn (3-2) to Sanford Stadium for a 3:30 p.m. ET showdown on ESPN. And this matchup could get ugly quickly. Kirby Smart's Bulldogs are coming off an impressive 20-17 road victory over Alabama, while Auburn suffered a disappointing 24-14 loss at Tennessee. Georgia has also won nine consecutive meetings against Auburn, including last year's 20-10 victory in Jordan-Hare Stadium. Georgia: The Bulldogs Are Built DIFFERENT Georgia might have delivered its most impressive performance of the season against Alabama. Despite missing its top two running backs, Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens, the Bulldogs rushed for 206 yards against one of the SEC's most talented defenses. Dwight Phillips Jr. stepped up in a major way, while Bo Walker provided additional production in the backfield. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was outstanding, completing 18 of 22 passes for 249 yards while accounting for two touchdowns. Through six games, Stockton has thrown for 1,298 yards and 14 touchdowns, completing more than 76% of his passes. Defensively, Georgia held Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell to just 185 passing yards while recording four sacks. With Chris Cole, Raylen Wilson, KJ Bolden, and Ellis Robinson IV leading the defense, Georgia has the personnel to completely overwhelm Auburn's offense. Auburn: Can the Tigers Even Keep This Competitive? Auburn enters Saturday with serious questions surrounding its offense. Quarterback Byrum Brown has thrown for approximately 1,055 yards with seven touchdowns and seven interceptions. While he's dangerous with his legs, his decision-making has been inconsistent. Against Tennessee, Brown rushed for 107 yards but threw two interceptions in the 24-14 loss. Wide receiver Keshaun Singleton has emerged as a reliable target, recording 29 receptions for 322 yards. However, Auburn's biggest concern might be its inability to consistently stop the run. Tennessee rushed for 237 yards against the Tigers last weekend. That's a terrible sign considering Georgia just rushed for more than 200 yards against Alabama without its top two backs. If Auburn can't contain Georgia's rushing attack, this game could be over by halftime. How Each Team Wins For Georgia, the formula is simple: establish the running game, control the line of scrimmage, and force Brown to beat its defense through the air. Stockton should have plenty of opportunities to attack Auburn's secondary once the Tigers begin loading the box. Defensively, Georgia must contain Brown's mobility and force him into obvious passing situations. For Auburn, everything starts with avoiding turnovers and creating explosive plays. Brown must use his legs to extend drives, while the Tigers' defense needs to generate pressure on Stockton. Auburn cannot afford to fall behind early and become one-dimensional. I don't see this game being particularly competitive. Georgia is coming off an emotional victory over Alabama, but Kirby Smart has built a program that rarely overlooks inferior opponents, especially rivals. The Bulldogs should dominate the line of scrimmage, and I expect another massive rushing performance regardless of whether Frazier and Bowens return. Stockton should have an efficient afternoon, throwing multiple touchdowns while Georgia's defense forces Brown into at least two turnovers. Expect the Bulldogs to establish a commanding lead before halftime and eventually begin rotating younger players into the game. Final Score: No. 1 Georgia 41, Auburn 10 Georgia dominates its oldest rival, improves to 7-0, and continues looking like the team to beat in college football. home.headline: Georgia Reveals Surprising Injury on Initial Report Which Could Have Huge Impact
home.blurb: While much of the focus has been on the weather, Wednesday evening revealed the initial injury availability report , and there was a significant Georgia player listed as out who nobody saw coming. Junior running back Chauncey Bowens, who was played an important role the last two seasons, is going to be out. The reports surrounding Bowens seem to indicate he was rolled up on during the win over Vanderbilt, with Dawgs Central even reporting that Bowens is in a walking boot this week. While the good news is that Nate Frazier is not on the report, one has to wonder just how healthy he is, and with Bowens now out, the Bulldogs all of the sudden look very thin at running back. Dwight Phillips Jr. -- who Kirby Smart has been heaping praise on the last couple of weeks -- will also undoubtedly be a key piece of the plan as well. Georgia has solid depth at the position, but Bowens being out along with Frazier likely being limited is a bit of a blow to the chances of winning the game. Bowens has been a key piece of the goal line attack with six rushing touchdowns on the year, and with 10 carries last week against Vanderbilt he led the attack. It was sophomore Bo Walker who made the most of his opportunities though with 71 yards on just five touches, and he is going to be a key piece this week as well. With weather conditions potentially brutal, establishing the run will be key, and an Alabama run defense that looks greatly improved this year certainly will love any edge they can get. More pressure is put on Gunner Stockton as well, but that's nothing he cannot handle. Injuries are a reality in this sport, and ultimately who manages them better can decide who is still standing at the end of a season. It's just another challenge for the Dawgs on a night that will be full of them, and Kirby Smart is being faced with one of the biggest regular season games of his career at Georgia. Time will tell how he and his team handle it.

Photo By - Reuters Connect. Alabama fans light up victory cigars to celebrate beating Tennessee. One of the SEC's best rivalry games returns for the 109th time since 1901, with Alabama and Tennessee playing at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC). A game known as the "Third Saturday in October" for when it's historically been played, the Crimson Tide had been dominating the Alabama vs. Tennessee rivalry during the Nick Saban era, but the programs have split the series over the last four years. Despite the Volunteers catching up to the Crimson Tide in recent seasons, Alabama is a 9.5-point favorite and the popular pick among college football analysts . Alabama vs Tennessee rivalry history: Third Saturday in October 60 (1 win vacated) 40 (1 win vacated) 15 (2007-2021) Longest win streak 7 (1995-2001) Largest margin of victory 992-346-43 (.734) Program record 892-424-55 (.671) Claimed national titles (recognized) Conference championships Heisman winners Consensus All-Americans Weeks in the AP Poll Weeks at No. 1 Bowl games (record) NFL draft picks First-round picks Alabama and Tennessee's rivalry has long been filled with winning streaks, legendary coaches, and cigars. The Crimson Tide and Volunteers played for the first time in 1901, with the programs tying 6-6 in Birmingham, Ala., the home of the rivalry for seven of the first eight meetings. However, the game wasn't initially played on the third Saturday in October (it was played in November), nor every season. For the first 26 years of the rivalry, Alabama and Tennessee played just 11 times, which included the teams not playing at all between 1915 and 1927. Over those first 11 meetings, Alabama went 8-2-1 and didn't allow a Tennessee touchdown from 1903 to 1913. The rivalry returned in full in October 1928, and Alabama and Tennessee have only gone without playing for one season since then, and that was in 1943 due to World War II. The return of the rivalry also coincided with Tennessee becoming a powerhouse under Robert Neyland, who was hired in 1926. That helped Tennessee turn it into a competitive rivalry, with the Volunteers going 20-15-6 from the 1920s through the 1960s. But that's when Alabama changed college football forever after hiring Texas A&M's coach, who had earned his nickname after agreeing to wrestle a bear when he was 13 years old. Paul "Bear" Bryant would beat Tennessee for the first time in 1961 and win on the third Saturday in October 16 times from '61 to '81, taking home six national championships in the process. The rivalry would resume its competitiveness in the 1980s thanks to Johnny Majors, with Tennessee owning Alabama in the 1990s under Phillip Fulmer. But then everything changed when Alabama brought the only college football coach better than Bryant to Tuscaloosa in 2007. Saban went 16-1 against Tennessee. But with Saban gone, the rivalry has been split the last two years under Kalen DeBoer. The first game between Alabama and Tennessee was on Nov. 28, 1901, in Birmingham, Ala. The two programs tied 6-6, the only time both teams scored points in the first 10 meetings. In 1901, Tennessee was held scoreless when Alabama won 24-0, and then the Volunteers shut out the Crimson Tide 5-0 in 1904. From 1905 to 1913, Alabama won seven straight against Tennessee, outscoring the Vols 112-0 (Tennessee would win 17-7 in 1914). After more than a decade-long hiatus, the rivalry returned in 1928 and became one of the top SEC rivalries thanks to Neyland. Why does the winner of Alabama vs. Tennessee smoke victory cigars? One of the most unique aspects of Alabama and Tennessee's rivalry is the victory cigars. The winning team lights up a victory cigar in its locker room following the game, and fans light them up in the stands of the stadium to celebrate a win. The tradition began in the 1950s when Alabama's athletic trainer Jim Goostree began handing out cigars following a win over Tennessee. Both programs continued the tradition, which began as a secret due to NCAA rules around extra benefits for players and use of tobacco products. In 2005, Alabama publicly brought the tradition back to the forefront of the rivalry but had to self-report it as an NCAA violation as a result. However, since 2007, the winner of Alabama vs. Tennessee has knowingly and openly violated the NCAA rule and reported said violation to the NCAA as part of the tradition. Why is it called the Third Saturday in October? This name is pretty self-explanatory, with Alabama vs. Tennessee being played on the third Saturday in October every season. The tradition began when Neyland started consistently scheduling the matchup against the Crimson Tide on the third Saturday in October, with the rivalry officially adopting the name of "Third Saturday in October" in 1939. Though the game hasn't actually always fallen on the third Saturday in October over the decades due to SEC scheduling and conference changes, the rivalry name of the "Third Saturday in October" has remained. Best moments in the Alabama vs Tennessee rivalry The Bear's streak ends (1982) Before Saban, there was Bryant, and the Bear didn't often lose on the third Saturday in October. When he initially took over Alabama in 1958, Bryant got off to a rough start against Tennessee, going 0-2-1. But between 1961 and 1981, Bryant was 16-4-1 against Tennessee, including an 11-game winning streak from 1971 to 1981. In 1982, Tennessee shocked the college football world after ending the streak. The Volunteers' legendary head coach Johnny Majors led his team to a 35-28 upset of No. 2 Alabama. Bryant would return for just one more season in Tuscaloosa, with Majors once again getting the best of the Bear, and Tennessee beating No. 11 Alabama 41-34. The five-overtime game (2003) Tennessee was looking to bounce back from a loss to Alabama in 2002, its first since 1994, in a clash that resulted in the longest game in the history of the rivalry. The No. 22 Volunteers came back from down 20-13 in the fourth quarter when Casey Clausen led a game-tying drive with 30 seconds left to force overtime. Tennessee managed to convert a 4th-and-19 to stay alive during double OT, and in the fifth OT, Clausen scored to pull off a 51-43 win in Tuscaloosa. The game lasted four hours and 53 minutes. The goalposts go for a swim when the drought ends (2022) One of the most improbable wins in the history of the Alabama-Tennessee rivalry came in 2022, when Saban was riding a 15-game winning streak (the longest in the rivalry's history) into Knoxville. Saban had owned the Vols for a decade and a half, recording double-digit wins in 13 of the 15 straight victories and handing Tennessee four of the largest blowout defeats in rivalry history. Essentially, Alabama proved they belong with the elite teams, with a resume boasting a win over the suddenly excellent Kentucky and a loss to #1 Georgia that could have gone either way. The Tennessee Volunteers are similarly 5-1, but it took squeaking out tight wins over SEC bottom feeders Arkansas and Auburn. The Vols have generally played well on defense, but their offense has left a LOT to be desired, with QB Faizon Brandon leading an anemic passing attack until he was injured, and backup George MacIntyre not doing any better. So they're sitting put with a #15 ranking. FanDuel's sportsbook has the opening odds set to Alabama holding a -6.5 favorite over Tennessee, with an over/under of 55.5. Week 1 – Beat Furman 56-9 Week 2 – Beat Georgia Tech 45-24 Week 3 – Beat Kennesaw State 42-9 Week 4 – Lost to Texas 17-20 Week 5 – Beat Auburn 24-14 Week 6 – Beat Arkansas 24-17 The Vols are averaging 22 points per game on offense and 17 points per game on defense in SEC play, with the biggest problem being that, for the season, they're averaging only 187 passing yards per game (and that includes their three warm up games to start the season). Running back DeSean Bishop is still carrying the entire offense with 678 rushing yards. Week 1 – Beat East Carolina 48-10 Week 2 – Beat Kentucky 45-17 Week 3 – Beat Florida State 50-36 Week 4 – Beat South Carolina 49-18 Week 5 – Beat Mississippi State 56-23 Week 6 – Lost to Georgia 17-20 The Tide's offense obliterated all of their first five foes, scoring 45+ in every single game despite having only a single cupcake game. Then Georgia happened, and the two elite squads turned the game into a low-possession, high-stakes contest (seriously, there were only 7 combined drives in the entire second half). The Alabama defense has had some struggles this year. They've been a playmaking defense, but they've also given up some downfield passes in almost every game, and then struggled with UGA's rushing attack last week. Still, the held the Dogs to less than half of their usual offensive output. Alabama boasts a much better offense, but the two teams have likely equivalent defenses. However, the game will be at Neyland Stadium. Still, the 6.5 spread with a 55.5 OU has the prediction something like a 31-25 Crimson Tide victory. How the Tide responds to a tough and disappointed loss in their clash with Georgia will be paramount, but I wouldn't be surprised if this one winds up going under the 55.5 points. Something more like a 21-14 kind of game. What do you think? Give us your thoughts in the comments below.

Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:42 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 6 Alabama travels to No. 14 Tennessee for a massive SEC rivalry showdown. Can Keelon Russell bounce back and keep the Tide's playoff hopes alive? One of college football's greatest rivalries returns Saturday afternoon as No. 6 Alabama (5-1) travels to Knoxville to face No. 14 Tennessee (5-1) in the Third Saturday in October showdown. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC, and both programs have plenty to prove. Alabama is coming off a heartbreaking 20-17 loss to Georgia, while Tennessee narrowly escaped Arkansas with a 24-17 victory. The Crimson Tide defeated Tennessee 37-20 last season, but the Volunteers have won the last two meetings in Knoxville. With both teams fighting for College Football Playoff positioning, Saturday's matchup could have enormous consequences. Alabama: Can Keelon Russell Bounce Back? Alabama's offense has been one of the nation's most explosive units, averaging 44.2 points per game. Quarterback Keelon Russell has thrown for 1,599 yards, 12 touchdowns, and just two interceptions while adding 225 rushing yards and four scores. However, Georgia exposed some weaknesses in the sophomore quarterback's game. Russell completed just 16 of 30 passes for 185 yards and one touchdown against the Bulldogs, struggling to consistently move the football against an elite defense. Saturday presents another difficult challenge. Tennessee is allowing just 15.5 points per game and has surrendered only three passing touchdowns through six games. Making matters worse, Alabama is expected to be without leading receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams, who has recorded 415 receiving yards and four touchdowns. That means Lotzeir Brooks, who has 389 receiving yards, and Rico Scott will need to step up. The Crimson Tide must also establish their rushing attack to prevent Tennessee from putting all its attention on Russell. Tennessee: The Volunteers Have a MAJOR Problem Tennessee has managed to win five of its first six games, but Josh Heupel's offense has serious questions at quarterback. Freshman Faizon Brandon has battled a shoulder injury, forcing George MacIntyre into his first career start against Arkansas. MacIntyre completed 18 of 29 passes for 247 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions. And against Alabama's talented secondary, those mistakes could prove extremely costly. The Volunteers rank just 110th nationally in passing offense, averaging 186.5 yards per game. However, Tennessee has been outstanding on the ground. Running back DeSean Bishop has rushed for 678 yards and eight touchdowns, helping Tennessee average 228.3 rushing yards per game. Bishop will be the biggest threat to Alabama's defense, especially considering Georgia rushed for more than 200 yards against the Crimson Tide last weekend. Wide receiver Mike Matthews, who leads Tennessee with 396 receiving yards, could also create problems if Alabama becomes too focused on stopping the run. How Each Team Wins For Alabama, the formula starts with forcing Tennessee to throw the football. If the Crimson Tide can contain Bishop and put the Volunteers into third-and-long situations, their defense should have opportunities to create turnovers. Offensively, Russell must protect the football, utilize his mobility, and attack Tennessee's secondary without forcing unnecessary throws. For Tennessee, everything revolves around establishing the rushing attack and controlling possession. The Volunteers must also generate consistent pressure on Russell and prevent Alabama from creating explosive plays downfield. A loud Neyland Stadium crowd could make things difficult for Alabama, particularly if Tennessee establishes an early lead. I expect a physical, defensive battle between two SEC rivals. Tennessee's rushing attack will create problems early, but I don't trust the Volunteers' quarterback situation against Alabama's defense. Whether it's Brandon or MacIntyre under center, Tennessee simply hasn't demonstrated enough consistency throwing the football. Russell should respond with a much cleaner performance after struggling against Georgia, although I don't expect Alabama's offense to put up its usual explosive numbers. The Crimson Tide will establish a narrow lead before halftime and gradually take control in the second half. I expect Alabama's defense to force multiple turnovers, while Russell makes enough plays to secure a comfortable road victory. Final Score: No. 6 Alabama 24, No. 14 Tennessee 13 Alabama gets back on track, improves to 6-1, and keeps its College Football Playoff hopes alive. Tennessee's quarterback struggles ultimately prove too much to overcome. Check Out All EasySportz College Football Content Here! College Football Viewing Guide

Known as " The Third Saturday in October ," this is a matchup that has produced mixed results in recent years after a dominant decade-plus stretch in the rivalry under former Alabama head coach Nick Saban. The teams have split the last four meetings between the two since 2022, with the home team winning in both Tuscaloosa and Knoxville. Both of those two Alabama losses in Knoxville have come in a pair of close games though, 52-49 and 24-17, both of which the Crimson Tide entered as the higher ranked team. Alabama struggled in multiple areas during both games, especially with penalties where they committed 17 and 15 in both, respectively. With the latest matchup also a Top 25 showdown similar to the previous two, can Alabama avoid a third-straight loss in Knoxville? Here is everything you need to know about the Volunteers ahead of Saturday's matchup. The Tennessee Vols will host the Alabama Crimson Tide this weekend in Neyland Stadium in a game that's very important for both programs. Tennessee and Alabama are both looking to move to 6-1 on the season. Whichever team wins this game will be in prime position to reach the College Football Playoff, while the loser will likely need to win out to secure a spot. The Vols have won the last two matchups in Knoxville. Former Georgia QB Aaron Murray predicts the final score of Alabama vs Tennessee Former Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Aaron Murray made his picks for some of this weekend's biggest games, including Alabama vs Tennessee. Murray, who was in the broadcast booth for the Vols' win over Arkansas last weekend, has Alabama getting the win in Knoxville on Saturday. Murray thinks the game will be somewhat close, but he's concerned about Tennessee's offense possibly being "one dimensional" against Alabama's defense. "Where's Bama at physically?" said Murray. "They got emotionally and physically, at times, beat up against Georgia last week. Linebackers were in the wrong gap, defensive linemen were getting displaced — Georgia running for a bajillion yards with a third string running back. "… But I really think Tennessee is in trouble of being a very one dimensional football team if they don't trust their quarterback in this game to kind of loosen things up. So I give the advantage right now to Bama until this coaching staff for Tennessee shows me they're willing to put more on the plate of whoever QB 1 is. So I like Alabama in this game. I like Alabama 24-14 ." The feeling is that sophomore George MacIntyre will start against Alabama, but true freshman Faizon Brandon is reportedly practicing this week, so he'll at least have a chance to play in this game. Tennessee and Alabama are set to kick off at 3:30 PM ET on Saturday in Knoxville. The game will air on ABC. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.headline: Alabama Football Injury Updates Against Georgia
away.blurb: UPDATE: Ryan Coleman-Williams is good to go for the second half, per a UA spokesperson. Nose tackle Terrance Green is questionable. Alabama cornerback Dijon Lee Jr. is slow to get up after a kick return midway through the second quarter and is immediately helped by the medical staff. He returned to the game on the Crimson Tide's next defensive drive. Alabama TE Josh Ford (game-time decision) is in uniform and with a cast on his left arm. Ford broke his arm last Saturday and got surgery on Sunday. He is expected to be available tonight vs. Georgia pic.twitter.com/vcgdi4EFmz Jorden Edmonds, DB — Game-time decision Josh Ford, TE — Game-time decision Ford is expected to be available to face Georgia, ESPN's Pete Thamel shared on College GameDay from Coleman Coliseum. Ford was reportedly doing pushups at practice on Tuesday despite the Sunday arm surgery. Alabama right tackle Jayvin James is not featured on the availability report. James left the Sept. 26 home win over South Carolina early with a lower extremity injury, and it forced him to sit out of the Mississippi State victory. Nevertheless, DeBoer said during Monday's press conference that he's "optimistic that [James] can return this week." He's good to go and is listed as the starting right tackle on the depth chart. It was reported a couple of weeks before the season that 5-star freshman cornerback Jorden Edmonds would miss some time due to a lower body injury. DeBoer said on Monday that "there’s a chance he can come back here, even in the regular season." That said, he was listed as questionable on the initial availability report. Edge rushers Justin Hill and Desmond Umeozulu have missed the Crimson Tide's past two games and they'll be out once again. Hill has a lower-extremity injury and Umeozulu has turf toe. Hill and Umeozulu are the second and third Wolf linebackers on Alabama's depth chart. DeBoer shared the latest on these two as well, stating that Umeozulu will take "probably a couple more weeks," and Hill will "be back this season, but more than likely not this week." away.headline: Alabama Head Coach Kalen DeBoer Shares Updates on Injured Tide Players Ahead of Tennessee Road Trip
away.blurb: "With Racin [Delgatty], just with his lower-leg injury, just continue to evaluate him and kind of see where he’s at in the days ahead. Obviously, he’ll be pretty sore, kind of working through things and limited, for sure, early in the week. Certainly get some reps with other guys, in particular, probably Mal Waldrep, Casey Poe, guys like that." "But I think going back to Ryan, I'm just gonna say this about all these guys that I mentioned, just Josh Ford last week, I mean, these guys go through things throughout the week that you don't see," DeBoer said. "And Ryan, in particular, has been doing that and leading the charge, not just with what he does to try to be out there on the football field for practice, but the energy and just trying to be an uplifting and uniting factor for not just the offense, but our football team. So, I know he was out there battling again on Saturday, giving everything he got, and he had until the very end.” Skip to main content Skip to site footer GET CONNECTED: TUSCALOOSA, Ala. -- Alabama lost three starters during its 20-17 loss to Georgia, with the Crimson Tide losing defensive lineman Terrance Green late in the first half, wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams on the final offensive drive, and center Racin Delgatty on the final drive. On Monday, Kalen DeBoer updated the statuses of all three of them, with Ryan Coleman-Williams likely to miss some time dealing with a couple of injuries. Here is what head coach Kalen DeBoer said about the three of them during his Monday media availability. "Ryan has a couple of things going on. Worked through an injury to his knee that's been kind of going on, and so we'll deal with that," DeBoer said. "Got the head issue as well. So, we’re gonna address that, even the lower-extremity there this week. Pretty good chance we wouldn’t have him here this weekend. I think he would be probably week-to-week after that." "And then Terrance [Green], just keep evaluating him. This is an injury that’s been going on for a couple weeks now. Just re-aggravated it, and it’s been limiting him in practice. And trying to get him to the game, he, I thought, made a great effort in trying to do that. Just, again, re-aggravated it." DeBoer also circled back on Ryan Coleman-Williams, Josh Ford, and the physicality and toughness that players like those two have shown this season. Offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb also said NC State transfer WR Noah Rogers is "pretty close" to 100% after his A-Day injury. Rogers played just one snap in the Tide's 20-17 loss to Georgia. No. 6 Alabama will travel to Neyland Stadium to take on the 14th-ranked Tennessee Volunteers on Saturday, October 17. Kickoff is scheduled for 2:30 p.m. CT on ABC. Can the Tigers pull off another upset, or will the Rebels defend Oxford? Two of the SEC's most intriguing teams are set to collide Saturday afternoon as No. 13 Missouri (5-1) travels to Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1). Both programs are coming off dominant victories. Missouri dismantled Texas A&M 27-6, while Ole Miss embarrassed Vanderbilt 52-17. With both teams sitting at 2-1 in conference play, Saturday's matchup could have major implications for the SEC Championship race and College Football Playoff. Missouri: The Tigers Are Legitimate Contenders Eli Drinkwitz has Missouri playing some outstanding football, particularly on defense. The Tigers are allowing just 17.7 points per game and rank eighth nationally in rushing defense, surrendering approximately 78 yards per contest. Offensively, former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns, and just one interception. Now, he gets an opportunity to prove himself against his former program. But Missouri's biggest weapon has been running back Jamal Roberts. Roberts has rushed for 828 yards and eight touchdowns, including consecutive 200-yard performances. Against an Ole Miss defense allowing 176.4 rushing yards per game, he could be in for another massive afternoon. Former Ole Miss wide receiver Cayden Lee has also been outstanding, recording 42 receptions for 616 yards and five touchdowns. If Missouri establishes its rushing attack early, the Tigers could control this game. Ole Miss: Can Trinidad Chambliss Carry the Rebels? Pete Golding has Ole Miss back in the national conversation following last season's historic playoff run. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss continues to be one of the most exciting players in college football, throwing for 1,435 yards and 11 touchdowns through five games. Wide receiver Deuce Alexander has emerged as his favorite target, recording 32 receptions for 503 yards and five touchdowns. The Rebels are averaging 38.8 points and nearly 434 yards per game, but their defense remains a major concern. Ole Miss is allowing 28 points per game, including an embarrassing 52-point performance against Florida earlier this season. And facing Missouri's balanced offense certainly won't make things easier. However, the Rebels have been outstanding at home, winning all three of their games in Oxford this season. How Each Team Wins Missouri must establish Roberts early and force Ole Miss into a physical, defensive battle. If the Tigers can dominate time of possession and limit explosive plays from Chambliss, they have an excellent opportunity to leave Oxford with a victory. For Ole Miss, everything starts with its passing attack. Missouri's defense has been elite against the run, meaning Chambliss will likely need to carry the offense. The Rebels must also force Simmons into mistakes and prevent Roberts from consistently reaching the second level. This matchup has all the ingredients for one of the best SEC games of the weekend. Missouri's rushing attack should give the Rebels serious problems, and I expect Roberts to surpass 100 yards once again. However, I trust Chambliss and the Ole Miss offense to deliver when it matters most. The Rebels' explosive passing attack, combined with a sold-out Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, should be enough to overcome Missouri's physicality. Expect a back-and-forth contest that comes down to the final minutes, with Chambliss engineering a late scoring drive to secure the victory. picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs. Missouri Preview: Rebels Face Tough Test Against Rising Tigers - SEC Country Skip to content Alabama Mississippi State South Carolina Instagram X-twitter Youtube Search Search Shop Alabama Stephan Stroud October 14, 2026 No. 9 Ole Miss will host No. 13 Missouri on Saturday afternoon in a major SEC matchup featuring two teams looking to strengthen their position in the conference race. The Rebels enter the game at 4-1 overall and 2-1 in SEC play after dominating Vanderbilt 52-17 last weekend. Missouri arrives in Oxford at 5-1 overall and 2-1 in conference action following an impressive 27-6 victory over Texas A&M. Kickoff is scheduled for 2:30 p.m. CT at Vaught Hemingway Stadium, with the game airing on the SEC Network. With both teams ranked inside the top 15, Saturday's matchup could be one of the most important games of the weekend. Trinidad Chambliss Leads Ole Miss Ole Miss will once again turn to quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , who has become the key part of the Rebels' offense. Latest episode SEC Country Podcast New shows Monday & Wednesday Airing It Out with Aaron Murray · Sep 25 The Rebels have shown that they can create explosive plays through the air, and Chambliss has played an important role in keeping the offense productive. Ole Miss will need another efficient performance from its quarterback against a Missouri defense that has been particularly strong against the run. The Tigers are allowing just 78.3 rushing yards per game, making it important for Chambliss to take advantage of opportunities in the passing game. Golding, who took over as Ole Miss head coach, will also want his offense to maintain the physicality and consistency it showed against Vanderbilt. Austin Simmons Returns to Oxford One of the biggest storylines will be Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons returning to face his former team . Simmons previously played for Ole Miss before transferring to Missouri, where he has become the leader of the Tigers' offense. Through five games, Simmons has thrown for 1,434 yards and 14 touchdowns. He has shown impressive arm talent and the ability to make plays outside the pocket, giving Missouri a quarterback capable of challenging opposing defenses in multiple ways. Simmons completed 14 of 28 passes for 147 yards and a touchdown against Texas A&M, helping Missouri secure a 27-6 victory. Although the passing numbers were not overwhelming, the Tigers controlled the game and delivered one of their strongest defensive performances of the season. Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz will look for Simmons to be more efficient against an Ole Miss team that knows his strengths and weaknesses. The familiarity between Simmons and his former teammates adds another layer to an already intriguing matchup. Eli Drinkwitz Has Missouri Rolling Drinkwitz has Missouri positioned for another important season in the SEC. The Tigers have combined a productive offense with a defense that has consistently made life difficult for opponents. Missouri is averaging 35.8 points per game while allowing just 17.7 points per contest. Running back Jamal Rogers has also become a major part of the Tigers' success, leading the SEC with 828 rushing yards entering the matchup. His ability to control the ground game could be especially important against an Ole Miss defense that has struggled to stop the run at times this season. The Tigers will look to establish Rogers early, allowing Simmons to work from manageable passing situations. A Major SEC Opportunity Ole Miss and Missouri both enter Saturday with plenty to prove. The Rebels want to build on their victory over Vanderbilt and demonstrate that they can compete consistently against ranked SEC opponents. Missouri hopes to continue its strong start and earn another important conference victory on the road. The quarterback matchup between Chambliss and Simmons will be central to the outcome, while the coaching battle between Golding and Drinkwitz adds another compelling storyline. With Missouri's rushing attack facing an Ole Miss defense that needs to remain disciplined, and the Rebels looking to exploit opportunities through the air, both teams will have important challenges to solve. Saturday's showdown in Oxford gives Ole Miss a chance to protect its home field, while Missouri arrives looking to prove its 5-1 start is no fluke.
