away.headline: Missouri football injury report Texas A&M: Tigers make 11 players available
away.blurb: Eleven of the 16 players who were on Missouri football's pregame availability reports between Wednesday and Friday were removed from the final pregame report, meaning all players who were not previously ruled out are available to play against Texas A&M. Mizzou had 16 players listed with five players listed as “out,” seven players listed as “questionable” and four players listed as “probable.” Now, the Tigers only have five players on the report, each of whom were already ruled out of playing against the Aggies. That means all of the following players should be able to play against Texas A&M: starting left tackle Cayden Green, starting defensive ends Langden Kitchen and Darris Smith, starting linebacker Robert Woodyard Jr., starting safeties Santana Banner and Kensley Louidor-Faustin, return specialist/wide receiver DaMarion Fowlkes, starting tight end Brett Norfleet, rotational cornerback Jahlil Florence, rotational defensive end Jaden Jones and backup linebacker Bobby Washington. The five players who were ruled out are running backs Ahmad Hardy and Malae Fonoti, backup safety JaDon Blair, reserve tight end Gavin Hoffman and right tackle Josh Atkins. The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable/game-time decision; doubtful; out. Texas A&M (3-2, 1-2) listed three players on its final report. Most notably, starting wide receiver Mario Craver is listed as a "game-time decision." Offensive lineman Blake Ivy and wideout Terry Bussey have been ruled out. This article originally appeared on Columbia Daily Tribune: Missouri football injury report Texas A&M: Tigers make 11 players available The SEC-mandated reports are required of member organizations every night beginning Wednesday in the leadup to an in-conference matchup, with the final report publishing 90 minutes before kickoff. Mizzou will kick off against Texas A&M at 11 a.m. Saturday on Faurot Field in Columbia. The game will air on ABC.

away.headline: Missouri's extensive injury report is looking increasingly like a nothingburger
away.blurb: The injury reports for Texas A&M and Missouri could not have looked more different coming into their huge game this morning, but it's looking more and more like that was all for show. The Aggies were down Terry Bussey (who is out for the season) and Blake Ivy, with Mario Craver listed as questionable, but it was the laundry list of players on Missouri's side that caught the eye of fans. The Tigers had listed as questionable players like star OL Cayden Green, starting S Santana Banner, and star Auburn transfer LB Robert Woodyard— in all, three of their top four tacklers on defense, as well as a remarkable number of offensive weapons. However, as game time has drawn nearer this morning, it looks like all of the hubbub around Missouri's potential missing players is possibly for naught. Reporting is emerging that some of the big time players for the Tigers that were listed as questionable in this game are on track to play, showing that the Aggies will indeed be facing a Mizzou team at nearly-full strength this week. Pete Thamel of ESPN reports that the Tigers' starting edge defenders, Darris Smith and Langden Kitchen, will both be playing against A&M in this game as well; both had been listed as questionable coming into the game. The game day update of the injury report confirms this from Thamel and Zenitz, as every single player that was listed as questionable or probable for the Tigers has been removed from the list , apparently set to play in this one. That's not only dismaying for the Aggies, it's a bit questionable on the part of the Tigers. We saw some interesting usage of the report by Lane Kiffin earlier this season, and though Eli Drinkwitz likes to do a bit of trolling from time to time, he doesn't quite have the same reputation as the LSU head coach does. While that's not an accusation that he was definitively misusing the report, it is odd that not a single player of the seven listed on the report as questionable actually will end up being unavailable for this game. That said, though, just because a player is not listed as "out" on this report does not mean that they are a sure thing to play in the game: we saw that with Jamarion Morrow last week for the Aggies. Texas A&M's optimism suddenly tamped down as Missouri's injury report apparently set to shrink Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports that Green, Banner, and Woodyard are all set to play in this game, which will be a huge relief for Tiger fans— but grim news for the Aggies, who definitely need all the help they can get in this one. In all, though, this means that Texas A&M will indeed have a challenge ahead of them today of a Tigers team at almost full strength. The Aggies need this win, but it was never going to come easy— this development only underlines that fact. away.headline: Ex-Rebels lead No. 13 Missouri into Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss
away.blurb: Simmons, top receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. weren't made available to speak Tuesday about transferring from Ole Miss, but it's worth noting that Simmons' Instagram account still has a number of posts from his years in Oxford. "I feel like those guys are definitely going to come out and play with a chip on their shoulder," tailback Jamal Roberts said. "We definitely can let them guys handle that." No. 9 Ole Miss reached the College Football Playoff semifinals a season ago with Trinidad Chambliss at quarterback after Simmons went down early with an injury and lost his starting job. Tigers coach Eli Drinkwitz acknowledged that the game will be a big deal for Simmons, along with two other Mizzou players imported from Ole Miss. Drinkwitz just wants them to keep perspective, considering about 20% of FBS players are transfers. "The biggest thing is to not make it bigger than it is," Drinkwitz told reporters Tuesday. "There are great memories from there. I think everybody left there in a positive light on both sides." "We talk about the joy of the journey," Drinkwitz said. "That was a part of their journey that made them who they are right now. I don't think there has to be a whole lot more to it than that." Mizzou (5-1, 2-1 Southeastern Conference) comes in having won two straight home games against SEC foes, most recently 27-6 over Texas A&M on Saturday. The Tigers' biggest win so far came against Florida, 45-17 on Oct. 3. Simmons has been terrific for the Tigers, ranking 11th in FBS in passing efficiency rating. He's completing 65% of his passes, with 14 touchdowns and one interception in 165 attempts. "He's playing as an experienced quarterback in a really good system," Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said. Lee has scored five touchdowns while leading the Tigers with 42 receptions and 616 yards. He and Simmons may be transfers, but they're already leaders at Mizzou, other players say. Roberts will be another focal point for Ole Miss. After putting together two straight games of 200-plus yards, he ranks first in the SEC and second nationally with 828 rushing yards. Mizzou's top back a season ago, Ahmad Hardy, is recovering from an offseason gunshot wound. Golding said that Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) will have its hands full trying to tackle Roberts. "He has the most yards after contact right now, which is something that has been an issue for us on tape," Golding said. With Chambliss continuing to rank as a Heisman Trophy contender and NFL prospect, Ole Miss routed Vanderbilt 52-17 on Saturday. The Rebels also have wins against ranked opponents LSU and Louisville. "They're a total team," Drinkwitz said. "We need to play our best, most complete game to even be in the game." away.headline: Injury update: Will Mario Craver play today for Texas A&M against Missouri?
away.blurb: Texas A&M star receiver Mario Craver has been listed as questionable all week against the Missouri Tigers, as he continues to recover from some bangs and bruises he has sustained throughout the season thus far. With the release of this morning's SEC Student-Athlete Availability Report , that status appears to remain for Craver with kickoff now under an hour and a half away. Craver is listed as a game-time decision for the Aggies in this report, meaning that fans will be sweating his status heading right up into the game. Craver's skill set makes him one of the toughest matchups for A&M's opponents on the entire team, so having him ready and available for the Aggies is key in this matchup. There are some positive signs for Craver going into this game, though: he was spotted heading out to warm up against the Tigers, potentially signaling that he will be ready to go. Warmups are warmups, but if he was trending towards not playing, this would not be happening. This is a similar pattern, though, to what we saw against Arkansas last week. Craver was listed as questionable throughout the week and called a game time decision against the Hogs, but he eventually was ready to go and saw a good number of snaps in the first half. He didn't play much of the later part of the game, as it looked like he had tweaked something in the touches he did get. Maybe that was out of a sense of safety, though, as the Aggies had the game well in hand by halftime, and were much more committed to the run than they were the pass against the Hogs. He eventually left the game with an apparent injury , though he did return later on in the contest. There was a similar story the following week against LSU, however: he was targeted a lot earlier on in the game, but eventually had to leave with some sort of injury before returning. Especially with Terry Bussey out, though, Craver's availability is paramount. There was a good showing from TK Norman last week, who looks ready to step into an increased role, but there's a big difference between Arkansas at home and Missouri on the road. Can the struggling Seminoles avoid another embarrassing defeat? One of college football's fiercest rivalries returns as No. 3 Miami (5-0) hosts Florida State (3-3) at Hard Rock Stadium. These two programs couldn't be heading in more different directions. Miami is coming off a dominant 41-13 victory over Clemson and remains firmly in the national championship conversation. Meanwhile, Florida State suffered an embarrassing 44-20 loss to Louisville after blowing an early 14-0 lead. With Miami entering as a heavy favorite, Mike Norvell and the Seminoles could be in serious trouble. Miami: The Hurricanes Look UNSTOPPABLE Mario Cristobal has built one of the most complete teams in college football, and quarterback Darian Mensah is playing like a legitimate Heisman Trophy contender. Mensah has thrown for 1,438 yards, 15 touchdowns, and zero interceptions this season. Miami is averaging an incredible 49.6 points per game while allowing just 9.8. Freshman sensation Malachi Toney has been nearly impossible to defend, recording 604 receiving yards and six touchdowns. His explosiveness gives Miami a dangerous weapon against a Florida State secondary that has struggled against quality competition. Running back Mark Fletcher Jr. provides another dimension to the offense, and Miami should have opportunities to establish the run against a vulnerable Seminoles defense. Florida State: Mike Norvell Is Running Out of Answers Florida State's season has quickly become a disappointment. The Seminoles allowed an unbelievable 397 rushing yards against Louisville, including 235 yards from Isaac Brown. That's a massive problem against Miami's balanced offense. Quarterback Ashton Daniels has thrown for 1,320 yards, eight touchdowns, and seven interceptions this season. Although Daniels has been dangerous with his legs, his inconsistency as a passer could become a serious issue against Miami's defense. Running back Ousmane Kromah has been productive with 565 rushing yards, but the Seminoles cannot rely entirely on their ground game if Miami builds an early lead. Florida State has enough athleticism to make some plays, but its defensive struggles and offensive turnovers make this an extremely difficult matchup. Defensively, the Hurricanes must contain Daniels' rushing ability and force him to win from the pocket. For Florida State, everything starts with controlling possession. The Seminoles must establish Kromah, limit Miami's explosive plays, and create turnovers. If Florida State allows this game to become a shootout, it could get ugly quickly. I simply don't see Florida State having enough answers for Miami's offense. Mensah has been outstanding, and I expect him to continue his Heisman-caliber season against a Seminoles defense that just surrendered 44 points to Louisville. Florida State should create a few explosive plays with Daniels and Kromah, especially early, but Miami's defense will eventually take control. I expect the Hurricanes to establish a comfortable halftime lead before completely taking over in the second half. away.headline: FSU Seminoles injury report: Latest updates ahead of Louisville
away.blurb: The FSU Seminoles did not make any changes to their availability report on Wednesday night, with 10 players still listed as out ahead of Friday's game against the Louisville Cardinals in L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium. Running back Sam Singleton Jr., wide receiver Devin Carter, defensive backs Karson Hobbs, Jamari Howard, Zae Thomas, and Jordan Crutchfield, and linebackers Blake Nichelson, Izayia Williams, Daylen Green, and Noah LaVallee are all out. Defensive lineman Darryll Desir is questionable. With linebackers Mikai Gbayor and Karon Maycock, defensive back Antonio Cromartie Jr., and punter Daniel Hughes all probable. Louisville made just one change on their report, with defensive back TJ Banks no longer listed after initially being listed as questionable. Starting quarterback Lincoln Kienholz is probable, along with defensive back Koen Entringer, defensive linemen AJ Green and Joshua Donald, and offensive linemen Ellis McAdoo and Anwar O'Neal. They will be without eight players, with defensive back Antonio Watts, punter Jacob Baker, wide receiver Montavin Quisenberry, tight ends Travis Egan and Hamilton Atkins, offensive linemen Bryten Close and Sam Secrest, and defensive lineman Sam Dawson all ruled out. Running back Keyjuan Brown, offensive lineman Cason Henry, and defensive lineman Daylen Russell are questionable. Added Cristobal: “The versatility that we were able to work with in practice and then actually use in the game has helped out a lot. Those guys are really highly intelligent, with real high normal IQs and football IQs. We have mixed and matched those guys every which way you can imagine. So that comes into play now and allows for competition to get ramped up.” It has worked out for Miami, with the Hurricanes leading the country in scoring defense (9.8 points allowed per game) and ranking sixth in total yards allowed per game (249.6). “I tell guys this ‘young guy’ stuff, throw that out the window,” Cristobal said. “You’re compensated. You’ve been here since January. Throw that out the window. Have maturity. Approach everything like a professional, and I think that approach has helped us develop a little bit faster, has accelerated some of that, so we’ll see what it looks like on game day.” The sophomore excelled in the new role, which didn’t surprise his coaches considering Fitzgerald’s ball-hawking nature and strong defensive instincts. So seeing everybody get those game reps and keep getting experience, it’s definitely amazing for the long run.” And was needed in the short run. Lucas and Brown are “all the way back” this week, according to coach Mario Cristobal, but those absences led to the Hurricanes using a lot of moving parts on the back end of the defense. Fitzgerald, who had a team-high six interceptions last season primarily playing safety and nickel, added outside corner to his repertoire. Omar Thornton has started all five games at nickel and has been stout in run defense and rushing the passer but needs to improve in pass coverage. home.headline: Hurricanes lose an offensive lineman to injury but get multiple defenders back
home.blurb: First, the bad news: Hurricanes sophomore offensive lineman Max Buchanan will be out for the immediate future, coach Mario Cristobal said Monday morning during his weekly radio hit on WQAM's The Joe Rose Show. He on Wednesday morning posted a since-deleted photo on social media of himself in a hospital bed with the caption "Y'all hold out .... [I'll] be back." The specific nature of the operation Buchanan underwent has not been publicly announced, nor has a timeline on how much time Buchanan is slated to miss other than Cristobal's vague "later in the year" comment on Monday. With Buchanan out for the time being, freshman Ben Congdon and sophomore SJ Alofaituli would be the most logical options to start at guard for Miami moving forward. Alofaituli started the first four games of the season at left guard opposite Buchanan. Congdon started in that spot against Clemson, with Alofaituli being Miami's primary right guard after Buchanan's injury. Cristobal on Monday afternoon said cornerback OJ Frederique Jr., who like Lucas was injured in the season-opener, won't return until "late" in the season. Miami had primarily relied on spot starter Ethan O'Connor and primary safety Bryce Fitzgerald to play outside cornerback the past four games because of the injuries to Lucas, Frederique, Brown and reserve cornerback Ja'Boree Antoine (who hasn't played yet this season). O'Connor and Fitzgerald have graded out as Miami's best defenders through the first five games of the season, according to Pro Football Focus. The Hurricanes already have three players who have been ruled out for the year in running back CharMar "Marty" Brown, wide receiver Josh Moore and tight end Luka Gilbert. home.blurb: More Videos MIAMI, Fla. – Coming off a bye week, the No. 3 Miami Hurricanes maximized the time off as several players are set to return from injuries; as head coach Mario Cristobal stated on The Joe Rose Show, “It paid off.” However, the same good news wasn’t shared about starting right guard Max Buchanan , who underwent surgery, which was revealed last Wednesday. He suffered a left knee injury against Clemson, but returned to finish the game. Buchanan has started in all five games thus far at right guard, as part of the Hurricanes’ reconstructed offensive line. Cristobal is hopeful he’ll be able to return later in the season – no specific timeline provided. Lightfoot left early in the first half of a 41-13 win over Clemson at Death Valley (Memorial Stadium). The rising star edge rusher has logged 19 total tackles, 11 solos and eight assists, 5.5 tackles for loss, and leads the program with five sacks thus far this season. picks.headline: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling
picks.blurb: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NLCS Game 3 updates NFL hot seats Champions League results Heisman Watch Story by Wildcats Wire Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 14, 2026 at 4:11 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels down to Norman to face the Oklahoma Sooners on Saturday, and both of these teams have plenty of momentum coming into this matchup. Arguably no team in the country has more momentum on their side than the Wildcats right now, coming off back-to-back walk off two-point conversions for the win in overtime. However, Oklahoma came off of their bye week and got a massive win over Texas in the Red River Rivalry game. With that being said, do not let the final score fool you, Oklahoma is still really struggling on offense. Oklahoma's offense will be the worst unit on the field this Saturday, and despite a big 27-24 win over Texas, the issues have not been fixed. The Sooners have scored just six offensive touchdowns since week two. They have only scored over 20 points twice this season, this was week one against UTEP and against Texas where they needed a blocked punt for a touchdown and a pick six to do so. This is a night game in Norman and will present a lot of adversity for Kentucky. The matchup to watch is the Kentucky offense versus the Oklahoma defense, but we will get into that side later. Basically every single offensive metric that you look at to determine offensive success, the Sooners rank bottom five in the SEC. Oklahoma ranks dead last in the conference in all of these statistics: Success rate, Rush SR%, EPA per rush, Explosive play rate and 1D+TD%. They also rank bottom five in the SEC in these statistics: EPA per play, EPA per dropback, Pass SR%, 3rd Down conversion rate, Early Down conversion rate and yards per play. This might be the worst offense Kentucky faces this season unless they can turn things around quickly. Oklahoma ranks first in the SEC in three-and-out rate and negative play percentage. The Sooners have the worst yards per carry average in the FBS. This is a stark contrast because Kentucky's defense ranks top five in the SEC in explosive % allowed and negative % forced. Kentucky's defense has excelled at three things this season: forcing turnovers, forcing negative plays and limiting explosives. This Oklahoma offense has struggled, but they do have some playmakers. The number one guy that should scare you, ironically, is number one Isaiah Sategna. Sategna is a dynamic receiver who is the one guy that can consistently create separation and he is dangerous with the football in his hands. Kentucky has to know where Sategna is on every snap because he is lightning in a bottle when he gets his hands on the football. John Mateer is a reckless but talented quarterback, he made the best throw of his season against Texas to set up the Sooners for the game winning field goal. Mateer threw a perfect back shoulder to Sategna from the far hash. Mateer has arm talent and is a dangerous runner, he immediately looks to run when a pass play breaks down. However, Mateer is extremely turnover prone, even moreso than LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt. Kentucky forced two turnovers on Leavitt, and they need to repeat that on Saturday. They have done a great job of forcing turnovers all season, they did it against Keelon Russell, Marcel Reed, LaNorris Sellers and Leavitt. This defensive line has to get pressure on Mateer to force him to play recklessly. The Wildcats have struggled with scrambling quarterbacks this season, but they were better last week against Leavitt--same thing applies this week with Mateer. Oklahoma as we stated, averages the fewest yards per carry in all of FBS. This is a game where Kentucky should be able to make Oklahoma one dimensional, which is a massive advantage for the Wildcats. The defense has to make Mateer uncomfortable in the pocket and they will have a great chance to win this football game. Kentucky's defense has the opportunity to have their best performance of the season this Saturday. What a wild Saturday it was for the Kentucky Football team. The Wildcats escaped with a 35-34 overtime victory over then-No. 10 LSU Tigers inside Kroger Field while rocking the iconic Power K jerseys. The game featured plenty of twists and turns, including trick plays that resulted in LSU touchdowns, explosive plays from Kentucky’s offense and special teams, turnovers, and, most importantly, missed field goals. Through it all, Kentucky remained competitive. With LSU facing a fourth-down situation late in regulation, the Tigers elected to punt rather than go for it. Kentucky then drove down the field in less than two minutes, setting up kicker Adam Zouagui for a field goal to send the game into overtime after he had missed his previous two attempts. Kentucky won the coin toss and elected to play defense first. LSU quickly drove down the field and scored a touchdown. The Wildcats then got their opportunity, and on third-and-10, quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Kenny Darby, who nearly took the ball into the end zone but came up a yard short. CJ Baxter immediately punched it in for a touchdown, leaving Kentucky down by one point. Instead of kicking the extra point to force a second overtime, first-year head coach Will Stein decided to go for the two-point conversion to win the game. The decision paid off. Minchey called his own number on a quarterback draw, found plenty of open space, and crossed the goal line untouched to secure the victory. Kentucky defeated LSU 35-34 in overtime, improving to 5-1 overall and 3-1 in SEC play. The Wildcats are now ranked No. 15 in the AP Top 25 poll. Oklahoma Sooners (3-2, 1-1 in SEC) The Oklahoma Sooners have faced increased scrutiny this season after finishing the 2025 campaign with a 10-3 record and earning a spot in the College Football Playoff. However, their season ended with a 34-24 loss to Alabama in the first round, and Oklahoma has struggled to find consistency this year. The potent offense Oklahoma showcased last season has largely been absent throughout the 2026 campaign. The exceptions came in the season opener against UTEP, when the Sooners cruised to a 51-0 victory, and this past weekend, when they defeated then-No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry. However, not all 27 points against Texas came from the offense. Oklahoma scored a touchdown after blocking and recovering a punt in the end zone, while another touchdown came on a pick-six. The Sooners’ other scoring plays included a rushing touchdown and two field goals. Across their other three games, Oklahoma has averaged just 12.3 points per game, which is disappointing for an offense expected to be productive under quarterback John Mateer. Speaking of Mateer, he has completed 90 of 135 pass attempts for a 66.7% completion rate, totaling 1,038 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Mateer is also a running threat, recording 53 carries for 70 rushing yards. Those numbers fall short of his previous two seasons in terms of passing production. In 2025, Mateer threw for 2,885 yards, while he recorded 3,139 passing yards in 2024. His touchdown-to-interception numbers also tell an interesting story. Mateer threw 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 2025, compared with 29 touchdowns and seven interceptions in 2024. For Oklahoma to defeat Kentucky, the Sooners will need Mateer to take another step forward and help their offense become more consistent. For Kentucky to win in Norman, Kenny Minchey and the offense will have to find a way to pierce the Sooners’ stingy defense and avoid game-breaking turnovers that won Oklahoma the game vs. then-No. 1 Texas. As for other notable Oklahoma players, the receiving corps features wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III, Mateer’s primary target, along with tight end Rocky Beers and wide receiver Trell Harris. Kentucky will need to account for all three playmakers while also limiting the Sooners’ running game, which features Lloyd Avant and Jonathan Hatton Jr. Game: Kentucky Football vs. Oklahoma Sooners Location: Oklahoma Memorial Stadium — Norman, Oklahoma Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 7:30 p.m. ET TV Info: SEC Network will have the TV broadcast Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a 6.5-point underdog . ESPN gives Kentucky a 32.1% chance of winning. Both teams could experience an emotional hangover after their big victories, but I believe Kentucky can overcome that challenge and earn another road win. "We needed to get a win for obvious reasons," OU coach Brent Venables said. "I want these guys to experience victory, certainly in this game was incredibly important." Fresh off their emotional Red River Rivalry upset , the Sooners are looking to carry the momentum into Saturday's home game against 5-1 Kentucky . The Wildcats knocked off LSU this past Saturday after converting a two-point try in overtime for the second straight week after UK did the same thing to defeat South Carolina. First-year Kentucky coach Will Stein has been one of the best stories in college football so far this season. OU scored on defense and special teams against the Longhorns and might need to do the same if it wants to win Saturday. The Sooners' offense scored only 13 points, totaling 238 yards but they seemed to find something in the run game with Lloyd Avant, while quarterback John Mateer took care of the football. "We’ve got a really good Kentucky team coming into Norman next Saturday night," Venables said. "Can’t go 8-0 until you go 1-0. Proud of our guys, proud of our coaches for their work, their fight and figuring it out and finding a way to get it done. Enjoy this for a few hours and get back to work. We’ve got a lot of improving. Several guys who didn’t play. They’re really good players. The Notre Dame transfer has completed over 67% of his passes for 1,394 yards, 11 touchdowns and only one interception. He has also been part of both two-point conversions, including his rush up the middle to beat LSU. The case for Kentucky: The Wildcats are no longer just a fun story. Stein has already equaled UK's win total from last season and has his team playing like a legitimate College Football Playoff contender. If Minchey continues to play clean football and Kentucky's defense can force Mateer into mistakes, it could be a long night for the Sooners in Norman. The case for OU: Momentum is a real thing. Maybe the Sooners' rivalry win helps them go on a similar run to that of last year's. Maybe offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle and Mateer will continue to improve. OU's defense has already proven it's one of the country's elite units and could be a problem for Minchey and the Wildcats. Not to mention the Sooners can create havoc on special teams. home.headline: Oklahoma Sooners' injury report for matchup vs. Texas Longhorns opened eyes to an issue that's been going on since 2024
home.blurb: The Oklahoma Sooners head into the Red River Rivalry against the Texas Longhorns with a long injury list. At this point, what's new? Banged-up rosters have become the norm for OU over the last few years. Ever since the SEC's player availability reports started in 2024, the Sooners have almost always carried a health disadvantage into game day. George Stoia of SoonersScoop.com pointed out a number that puts it in perspective, and I think it's worth mentioning. Stoia laid it out: OU averages 10.25 players on the initial availability report since it began in 2024. Its opponents averaged 6.68. OU has had fewer players on the initial report only once-the College Football Playoff game against Alabama. The Sooners had 6 players on that report. That feels about right. Nobody needs to stat-check it, either. Thursday's availability report for OU vs. Texas tells the same story . The Sooners have five players listed as out, two doubtful, one questionable, and five probable. Oklahoma – Out: Taylor Heim, Trell Harris, Xavier Robinson, Jacobe Johnson, Fred Hinton – Doubtful: Trynae Washington, Michael Fasusi – Questionable: Eddie Pierre-Louis – Probable: Jer'Michael Carter, Cole Sullivan, Michael Boganowski, Owen Heinecke, Jack Van Dorselaer. Texas – Out: Kaliq Lockett, Jordan Coleman, Zion Williams – Questionable: Justus Terry That's 13 names for Oklahoma and four for Texas. That's just how it is for the Sooners every week. When the Wednesday report came out, some fans were legitimately concerned. The list looked worse than it did heading into the Georgia game, even though OU had a bye week in between. More names showed up after a week off, not fewer. So fans scrambled to figure out how a team gets more injured during a bye. Fair enough, that's a decent question to ask. How does that work? I have no idea. Most likely, some players got more banged up in the Georgia game, and we just didn't know about it going into the bye. That's why building depth in the NIL era matters so much. You're going to have injuries, and OU seems to have more than anybody. Maybe that perception is right, maybe it's wrong. Regardless, the depth has to be better. You can sit here and look at this issue all you want and try to figure out what's going wrong internally. The game still has to be played. Texas isn't going to skip the Red River Rivalry because Oklahoma has a lot of guys on the report. You'd love to see the Sooners keep building their depth so the next man up can carry more of the load. For now, the Longhorns definitely have the advantage. Texas is already the No. 1-ranked team in the country, and the Sooners are coming in with really bad football. With 13 players on the availability report, OU will need its backups to step up. picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska football is hitting the road for one of its biggest games of the season, and Adam Carriker is breaking it all down on the Carriker Chronicles! Matt Rhule and the Nebraska Cornhuskers are heading to Eugene to face Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks in a late-night Big Ten showdown. Both teams are coming off losses, and both have plenty to prove. Can the Huskers bounce back and pull off an upset? Nebraska enters the game at 5-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Curt Cignetti and Indiana. The Huskers showed some good things against the Hoosiers, but once again, they couldn't finish the job. Carriker discusses why Nebraska needs more than another moral victory. At some point, the Huskers have to start winning these big games, especially against talented Big Ten opponents. One of the biggest questions is whether Anthony Colandrea and Nebraska's offense can get things going against Oregon's defense. Colandrea has shown he can make plays, but Carriker believes offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen needs to put him in good situations, especially on third downs. The Huskers also need production from Jamal Rule and the running back rotation. Can Nebraska establish a running game and keep Oregon's defense guessing? On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's Blackshirts face a major challenge. Oregon has talented receivers who can stretch the field and create explosive plays. Carriker looks at Nebraska's defensive numbers and explains why the Huskers cannot allow Oregon to make big plays over the top. The Blackshirts have been improving, but this will be another serious test of just how far they've come. Carriker also breaks down Oregon's defense, including players like Matayo Uiagalelei and Bear Alexander. The Ducks have plenty of talent, but Oregon has also been unpredictable this season. Nebraska cannot afford to let this become the game where everything suddenly clicks for Oregon. This is also Nebraska's stiffest road test so far this year. Playing in Eugene, in front of a loud Oregon crowd, will test the Huskers' experience and mental toughness. Nebraska has added veteran players who have been through big games before. Now it's time to see whether that experience pays off. Carriker shares his four keys to the game: handle Oregon's crowd, execute in the red zone, prevent big plays and play all four quarters. Nebraska must protect Colandrea, finish drives and avoid the mistakes that have cost the Huskers in close games. Finally, Carriker discusses the point spread and makes his score prediction! He's picking Nebraska to pull off the upset, 24-21! Can Matt Rhule and the Huskers shock Oregon, earn their third Big Ten win and make a statement to the rest of college football? Or will Dan Lanning and the Ducks send Nebraska home with another disappointing loss? Get Adam Carriker's full Nebraska-Oregon preview, breakdown and prediction on the Carriker Chronicles! picks.headline: 'I Will Ride or Die with Anthony Colandrea': Matt Rhule Recaps Nebraska's Loss to Indiana, Previews Oregon
picks.blurb: 'I Will Ride or Die with Anthony Colandrea': Matt Rhule Recaps Nebraska's Loss to Indiana, Previews Oregon Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska head coach Matt Rhule knows 55 minutes of good football isn't enough. It might be against some teams, but not most. As the Huskers look to bounce back from a three-point loss to defending national champion Indiana , Rhule and his staff are making that a point of emphasis for the entire team. At the same time, Rhule is willing to bet on his quarterback to get the job done. Meeting with the media Monday, Rhule reiterated that message and shed light on the Big Red's preparations for its Week 7 road game against the Oregon Ducks. Here's everything he had to say. Anthony Colandrea looks to pass against Indiana. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NU led for much of the game Saturday afternoon, yet the Hoosiers came crawling back. Even when Indiana took the lead late in the fourth quarter, Rhule was still willing to bet on Colandrea to make a play. NU led for much of the game Saturday afternoon, yet the Hoosiers came crawling back. Even when Indiana took the lead late in the fourth quarter, Rhule was still willing to bet on Colandrea to make a play. Asked about going for it on fourth-and-nine, the head coach pointed to what the analytics said: Go for it. It didn't work out this time, but he said he'd do it again. “I just felt like I was going to follow the analytics and put the ball in Anthony’s hands,” Rhule said. “We had holes that we thought were open and felt like, if we wanted to win that game, that ball and that field position, when you needed about 20 yards to kick a field goal, I’m going to put it in Colandrea's hands.” “I don’t always follow the analytics,” he continued. “I felt like our defense would get the stop, but more importantly, I just felt like I needed to put this ball in my guys' hands. I will ride or die with Anthony Colandrea all day, every day.” Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti and FOX Sports' Joel Klatt walk on the sideline during warmups before Saturday's game. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There's no shame in losing to perhaps the best coach in college football in 2026. Still, Nebraska had the Hoosiers on the ropes and failed to put them away. There's no shame in losing to perhaps the best coach in college football in 2026. Still, Nebraska had the Hoosiers on the ropes and failed to put them away. Rhule knows the Huskers need to be better in a few key moments, like that fourth-and-nine, but he doesn't believe the team needs to overhaul much. “When we watched the tape on Sunday, I think you have a team that is angry, who knows they let one get away,” he said. “We’re certainly disappointed, but not discouraged. We also understand that that is what it looks like. You have to not play really well for 55 minutes, you have to play well for 60.” “I think each and every one of us: coaches, staff, players, knows that we have to be one or two plays better,” he continued. “I’ve encouraged the guys to take this time to be one or two plays better, every one of us, so that we can win that game when it comes back in the future.” Kyle Cunanan kicks a PAT last season. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The offense wasn't the only unit that missed an opportunity to make a play. Nebraska's special teams failed to convert a 40-yard field goal late in the first half, a miss that proved costly in the three-point loss. The offense wasn't the only unit that missed an opportunity to make a play. Nebraska's special teams failed to convert a 40-yard field goal late in the first half, a miss that proved costly in the three-point loss. Even so, Rhule still has confidence in his specialists. NU is just 3-for-7 on field-goal attempts in 2026, but the Huskers' head coach said a strong week of practice would influence his decision to trust the kicking game moving forward. “I don’t know if it was perfect, but that’s one we should make,” said Rhule. “I think we’ve had our share of issues so far… We had a missed extra point against Maryland. We had a bad snap against Maryland… I can’t live in a world of confident (or) not confident. I have to err on the side of going for it.” “If we have a great week of practice, then I’ll lean towards that (kicking),” he continued. “But with Anthony, we basically have been like, ‘Hey, we’re going to try to play four downs’. Not because we don’t trust our field goal game, but because we believe in the weapons we have on offense… But yeah, it’s just something we’ve got to get cleaned up this week before we go to Oregon.” Football out west. 🗓️ 10.17.26 ⏰ 10:00 PM CT 🏟️ Autzen Stadium vs Oregon 📺 @CFBONFOX pic.twitter.com/Cy6UNrS913 Nebraska's game at Oregon will feature the latest kickoff time Rhule has ever coached, with the game certain to extend into the early hours of Sunday morning Central time. To prepare for that, NU is pushing its practices back a two hours and asking players to adjust their sleep schedules. “I had read some of the things that P.J. Fleck had done, I had read some of the things that Charles Huff at Memphis had done, and a lot of it just goes into sleep,” he said. “We’re really asking our guys to go to bed a little bit later each night this week.” “We’re going to finish this game at 2 a.m. our time,” he continued. “Your circadian rhythm starts to shut down, so we’re really just trying, as best as we can, to make 2 a.m. become 12 a.m., make 12 a.m. become 10 p.m. in terms of our bodies this week.” Anthony Colandrea carries the ball against Indiana. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Having a veteran team likely helps, but so does having a quarterback who sets the tone for the entire team. Colandrea, who carried the ball 17 times for 47 yards and a touchdown Saturday, is one player Rhule probably won't have to worry about getting ready to play. Having a veteran team likely helps, but so does having a quarterback who sets the tone for the entire team. Colandrea, who carried the ball 17 times for 47 yards and a touchdown Saturday, is one player Rhule probably won't have to worry about getting ready to play. Despite Colandrea's heavy workload in Week 6, Rhule maintained his stance on trusting the quarterback to remain productive while making smart decisions to protect his health. "I want him to play," said Rhule. "Dante (Moore, Oregon's quarterback) got hurt sliding, you know? Other guys are getting hurt sliding as well. Would I like Anthony to run the ball out of bounds? Certainly, but he's also cutting back on the zone read and making that game 17-6." "If you have a Porsche, you better let it drive 180," he continued. "I know everything I say gets blown into a little tidbit; I'm not saying he's a Porsche; I'm just saying I think it would be unwise to have a player like Anthony and not let him play to his full ability." picks.headline: 'An Opportunity Missed': Nebraska Defensive Coordinator Rob Aurich Recaps Indiana Loss, Previews Oregon
picks.blurb: 'An Opportunity Missed': Nebraska Defensive Coordinator Rob Aurich Recaps Indiana Loss, Previews Oregon Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska had Indiana bottled up until they didn't. College football games last 60 minutes for a reason, and the Cornhuskers ultimately couldn't hold on to a two-possession lead in the fourth quarter. As Nebraska defensive coordinator Rob Aurich prepares his unit for a road matchup against a capable Oregon offense Saturday night, he met with the media Tuesday to recap the Blackshirts' performance against the Hoosiers and preview the challenge ahead against the nation's 25th-ranked offense. Aurich knows his defense played well for much of Saturday's game. Even so, he sees an opportunity for the Blackshirts to learn from what went wrong. “An opportunity missed,” he said. “Haunting a little bit, but don’t let the game beat you twice. You take what you can; you learn from it. First year with these guys. I think it’s an excellent opportunity for us to understand what winning time is and how we perform in those moments.” As the Huskers prepare for Oregon, they'll need to make plays in critical moments to have a chance to pull off the upset. Indiana running back Lee Beebe Jr. is tackled by Nebraska defensive lineman Anthony Jones Jr. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Despite the loss, there was plenty that went right for the Big Red. Perhaps the most impressive takeaway was Nebraska's ability to shut down Indiana's running game. Despite the loss, there was plenty that went right for the Big Red. Perhaps the most impressive takeaway was Nebraska's ability to shut down Indiana's running game. “I think we’ve taken steps,” he said. “Fundamentally, you’re seeing us play different coverages at a higher level and have a bunch of answers for some teams with a pretty hefty run game.” “Gonna be another great test this week,” he continued. “I think Oregon has a lot of great tools in the run game that we’re going to have to match up with well. I’m pleased where we are, but I don’t think we’re anywhere near where I think we can be still.” Oregon Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola carries the ball against UCLA. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Oregon's running back duo of Jordan Davison and Dierre Hill won't be the only matchup for Husker Nation to watch. The two backs have combined for 529 yards and nine rushing touchdowns through five games, but the Ducks also have several quarterback options who could see the field. Oregon's running back duo of Jordan Davison and Dierre Hill won't be the only matchup for Husker Nation to watch. The two backs have combined for 529 yards and nine rushing touchdowns through five games, but the Ducks also have several quarterback options who could see the field. Still, Aurich knows Oregon will maintain its offensive identity regardless of which quarterback earns the start. “At the core of who they are, they’re going to be who they are,” said Aurich. “They’re going to be 11 and 12 (personnel); they’re going to have play actions off of that. They’re going to have a little bit of RPO free access. They want to get their playmakers involved.” “As we navigate each quarterback, I don’t know if it’s necessarily adding this plan to here, but we pull the best matchups from what we plan against all their core stuff,” he continued. “It’s much more of a where on the call sheet are we pulling from rather than a separate plan (for each quarterback).” Ohio wide receiver Eian Pugh is tackled by Nebraska's Jamir Conn. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Like the Ducks, Nebraska is dealing with injuries as it enters the back half of its 2026 schedule. Like the Ducks, Nebraska is dealing with injuries as it enters the back half of its 2026 schedule. Most notably, starting safety Jamir Conn's availability remains a question. On Monday, head coach Matt Rhule called Conn the "lifeblood" of Nebraska's defense . If Conn can't play, Aurich said the solution won't necessarily be as simple as plugging in his backup. In fact, the Big Red may even dabble in different defensive packages. “As we kind of iron out what Jamir’s availability is going to be, if he’s not available, it’s going to be a great test for everybody else in that room,” said Aurich. “Who steps up and how we find the best combination of the best 11 players on the field.” “Let’s say, for whatever reason, someone wasn’t available; it’s not always that we have to replace them with a safety or a corner,” he continued. “What’s the best 11?” Defensive lineman Owen Stoudmire | Nebraska Athletics Given how well Nebraska's defensive line played against Indiana, the Huskers could look to add another player at the line of scrimmage Saturday night. Aurich didn't say that directly, but he praised several defensive linemen for their performances. Given how well Nebraska's defensive line played against Indiana, the Huskers could look to add another player at the line of scrimmage Saturday night. Aurich didn't say that directly, but he praised several defensive linemen for their performances. “He’s the man,” Aurich said of Boston College transfer Owen Stoudmire. “He’s like a centering force of that defensive line. There are a lot of personalities on the defensive line, in a great way, but Owen is just steady, man. He’s steady and doesn’t get moved.” Aurich also praised freshman defensive tackle Dylan Berymon for making an impact in a high-stakes game. “I’m jacked up that he came and impacted us, not in garbage time, in a Big Ten game,” he said. “Really, really pleased with him. I think you’re going to see his role continue to expand.” Football out west. 🗓️ 10.17.26 ⏰ 10:00 PM CT 🏟️ Autzen Stadium vs Oregon 📺 @CFBONFOX pic.twitter.com/Cy6UNrS913 Whether Nebraska opts for a different defensive scheme or adjusts its personnel in the secondary, the Huskers will face one of the nation's most explosive offenses this week. The Nebraska Cornhuskers took the defending champion Indiana Hoosiers to the wire, leading for over three quarters before eventually falling 20-17 to the top five team. But sadly, it wasn't meant to be for Anthony Colandrea (pictured above, pointing to Will Compton en route to a 39-yard touchdown that put the Huskers up 17-6, seemingly icing the game for Big Red) and Company, as Herbert Hoover found Nick Marsh for two fourth-quarter scores, keeping the visitors from Bloomington unbeaten. It was, of course, Nebraska's first loss of the season. This team will go the way of its quarterback. How far can Anthony Colandrea carry the Nebraska Cornhuskers? That depends on if every defense will drop eight into coverage and rush three. Three of those eight in coverage are likely SPIES working for the enemy. Well, spies spying on our beloved quarterback. AC also had a few bad throws, struggling to feed his receivers catchable passes. For the first time this season, Nebraska did not throw a touchdown pass. The running game barely scraped by the century mark. Big plays crushed the defense. But if you looked at this game and don't see progress, you're being willfully ignorant. The Huskers controlled the ball, nearly doubling the time of possession. Nebraska was the more physical team, and the defense shut down two prominent opposing rushers. Now Big Red travels to Eugene to face the Oregon Ducks. Oregon just lost to UCLA, benched Dylan Raiola for a former walk-on, and was bumped from the Top 25. Needless to say, it's been a big week for the Ducks. Let's look at what the experts are saying. Vegas oddsmakers believe that this is a much better Nebraska team than what they predicted in the summer. Before the season, the spread for this game was 21.5 points. Immediately after the Nebraska/Indiana game, the spread was 12.5 points. Then Oregon lost to the Bruins. As of this writing, the FanDuel Sportsbook has the home Ducks as a 7.5-point favorite. The Over/Under is currently set at 52.5 points. Put the coffee on for a long night. Nebraska and Oregon kick off at 10:00pm Central Saturday night.

picks.headline: 4 bold predictions as Oregon football looks to rebound vs. Nebraska
picks.blurb: News Sports Entertainment Life Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL 4 bold predictions as Oregon football looks to rebound vs. Nebraska Alec Dietz Eugene Register-Guard Oct. 14, 2026, 9:01 a.m. PT Oregon football will face Nebraska at home on Saturday, aiming to recover from a recent loss to UCLA. The Ducks are favored, but Nebraska's defense, which ranks in the top 25 nationally, poses a significant challenge. Oregon's quarterback situation is uncertain, with Dante Moore's status unclear due to injury. The Oregon football team , looking to get its season back on track and keep its dwindling College Football Playoff hopes alive following a 17-15 loss to UCLA last weekend , will have just that chance vs. Nebraska Saturday, Oct. 17 at Autzen Stadium. In a rare true night game, the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten Conference) will take on a Cornhuskers (5-1, 2-1) squad looking for an upset after coming oh-so-close against Indiana at home last weekend. UO is just more than a touchdown favorite as of Wednesday. "They're playing really, really great on defense," Oregon coach DAn Lanning said. "Very aggressive. They're a good tackling team, they don't give up long runs ... it's a really talented group that we're going to have to play really well for. I know we'll have a great crowd, night game, so that'll be a fun environment for us to be a part of." Oregon vs. Nebraska scouting report Why Oregon has an advantage: Though the Ducks are reeling, especially offensively, Nebraska's offense has been unsteady against better teams, which could play into another tight contest come Saturday. The Cornhuskers are 5-9 since 2023 in Big Ten road games and have been hit or miss against the better teams on their schedule. They took a 10-point second-half lead over Indiana before a late Hoosier comeback. Despite a dismal showing against UCLA, the Ducks still have a top-10 passing offense in the country and take on a somewhat susceptible Cornhusker passing defense. Why Nebraska has an advantage: The Cornhuskers might have lost against the defending champs last week, but proved they could play with the best teams in the country after a 5-0 start to the season. The Ducks, meanwhile, need a big boost of energy after a lethargic showing against UCLA. Nebraska is likely the more confident group and could pounce at the opportunity of attacking a down Oregon team. The Cornhuskers also have one of the best defensive units in the country through six games, ranking in the top 25 in the country in total defense, better than a UCLA group that stymied Oregon last week. Oregon vs. Nebraska injury updates Note: Official availability reports, mandated by the Big Ten, are released every day starting at 5 p.m. Wednesday leading up to kickoff. This story was published before the reports are made public. For Oregon: The good news for Oregon is seemingly, no player suffered a substantial injury in its loss to UCLA last weekend. The bad news is several key contributors were listed as out, including quarterback Dante Moore, with no clear timetable for return. Starting safety Aaron Flowers was also listed as out and Jeremiah McClellan sat with an injury sustained during warmups against Portland State. McClellan is expected to miss much of the season while Moore (concussion) and Flowers' status will be more clear Wednesday. For Nebraska: The Cornhuskers may face the Ducks without one of their best defensive backs in Jamir Conn, who left Nebraska's loss against Indiana with a chest injury and was seen in a sling on the sideline. Key defensive lineman Riley Van Poppel was listed as questionable through the week heading into the game but sat out the loss, as well. It's unclear whether either of those players will be ready to go against the Ducks. Oregon vs. Nebraska: 4 bold predictions If Dante Moore can't play, Dylan Raiola will start against his former team at quarterback Let it be known that Lanning doesn't allow any outsiders at practice. We can only make predictions based on what we've seen in games and what coaches and athletes tell us, so our guess is as good as anyone's who follows along. But if Dante Moore is still recovering from his concussion and is held out against Nebraska this weekend, Dylan Raiola gives Oregon the best chance to win, at least from the onset. Raiola started 22 games for the Cornhuskers before transferring to Oregon and is a former five-star prospect with all the right tools to succeed. He threw for nearly 300 yards and two touchdowns against USC before an absolute stinker against UCLA. Though Brock Thomas gave the Ducks life in the fourth quarter, we think Raiola will get the first nod again, with a much shorter leash if things turn sideways. Oregon's success on first down will determine how its offense performs The Ducks were putrid in almost every aspect through three quarters against UCLA, at least offensively. Worse than maybe everything was how little Oregon managed on first down, leading to third-and-longs it couldn't convert. The Ducks finished 1 for 14 on third- and fourth-down conversions and averaged just 4.4 yards per play. That has to change Saturday, starting with first down players that get the Ducks off to a better start and more manageable later downs. If Oregon can create success on first down and stay on schedule, its offense should see a substantiative boost. Nebraska's Anthony Colandrea will be a much stiffer test than UCLA's QBs With respect to Nico Iamaleava and Ty Dieffenbach, Oregon will be facing a much better quarterback this weekend, at least statistically, in Nebraska's Anthony Colandrea. The senior and UNLV transfer has completed 64% of his throws for 1,406 yards, 13 touchdowns and just three interceptions in six games and rushed for nearly 300 yards and three scores. Colandrea is a true dual-threat playmaker, an QB archetype that Oregon has struggled with this season. Though the Ducks have played good QBs this season like Drew Mestemaker and Jayden Maiava, Colandrea is no slouch and will have success against Oregon's defense Saturday, at points. The Cornhuskers opened with five consecutive victories, including an impressive 48-23 win over Maryland, before facing undefeated Indiana on Saturday. Nebraska came close to earning a significant conference victory but ultimately fell 20-17 after Indiana completed a late comeback. The defeat was frustrating, although the Cornhuskers demonstrated enough quality to suggest they can compete against some of the conference’s stronger opponents. The performance against Indiana was particularly encouraging because Nebraska controlled several important statistical categories. The Cornhuskers generated 391 total yards compared with Indiana’s 328 and held possession for more than 39 minutes. Nebraska also ran 83 offensive plays while limiting Indiana to just 44, demonstrating an ability to control the tempo and prevent an explosive opponent from establishing sustained pressure. However, the Cornhuskers couldn’t convert that statistical advantage into enough points, allowing Indiana to remain competitive before taking the lead late. Nebraska has averaged 39.2 points per game while allowing just 15.2, numbers that reflect a team with considerable balance on both sides of the football. The Cornhuskers have also demonstrated effective rushing production, which could become particularly important against an Oregon defense that has struggled during portions of its schedule. Saturday presents a difficult road challenge at Autzen Stadium, but Nebraska’s performance against Indiana suggests the team should be capable of remaining competitive if it avoids costly mistakes. The Ducks also experienced difficulty establishing a consistent rushing attack, preventing them from controlling possession during important stretches. Returning to Autzen Stadium provides Oregon with an opportunity to regroup, particularly against a Nebraska team coming off its own disappointing defeat. away.blurb: The loss dropped the Ducks out of the rankings thanks to a 3–2 record. Oregon will face the Nebraska Cornhuskers on Saturday, but it remains to be seen who will start at quarterback this weekend amid Dylan Raiola's struggles and the status of Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in Oregon's 41–27 win over USC on Sept. 26. Oregon HC Dan Lanning Playing Coy on Dante Moore's Status Against Nebraska - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Oregon HC Dan Lanning Playing Coy on Dante Moore's Status Against Nebraska (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Jordan Sigler Wed, October 14, 2026 at 9:56 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Oregon Ducks are in desperation mode this week after losing 17–15 to the UCLA Bruins in Week 6. On Wednesday, Ducks head coach Dan Lanning played coy with the media, opting not to go into detail about the quarterback position this week. Per Zachary Neel of Ducks Wire, Lanning said he wouldn't reveal Moore's status until it was placed on the Big Ten availability report. Lanning did add that Moore has been practicing this week and looks the part. Moore played inconsistently through his first four starts this season, completing 69.7 percent of his passes for nine touchdowns and no interceptions. away.headline: Riley Van Poppel injury threatens Nebraska where Indiana can hurt it most
away.blurb: Considering that Van Poppel looked like he wasn't adjusting all that well to Aurich's defense in fall camp and then surged into a situation where he was getting as many snaps as any defensive lineman in the last few weeks, it couldn't be a worse time for an injury to keep him out of Saturday morning's massive game. The good for Nebraska heading into the massive showdown against Indiana on Saturday is that the team is mostly healthy. Jamal Rule, Jacory Barney, and Mekhi Nelson are off the injury reports entirely. The bad news is that Thursday night's report added a defensive player the Huskers can scarcely afford to miss. Riley Van Poppel's apparent injury isn't a big deal simply because he's a defensive lineman, and the Hoosiers' run game is easily the best the Huskers have faced so far this year. His potential absence is also a big issue because Van Poppel's playing time has increased as the season has gone on. Van Poppel's use by Nebraska defensive coordinator Rob Aurich has, in fact, never been bigger than it has been since Nebraska started Big Ten play. Against Ohio, he saw just 30 snaps. Against Bowling Green, it was down to 18, and he had just 28 snaps against North Dakota. However, he tallied 46 snaps against Michigan State and 44last week against Maryland. Riley Van Poppel injury could weaken Nebraska football front against Indiana running backs Van Poppel hasn't always been on the stat sheet. He has just 7 tackles, but 2 of those were sacks. He's also got 9 quarterback pressures, including 5 in Big Ten games alone. While his 2 sacks came in non-conference play, he's shown he can make an impact in the trenches, with 2 quarterback hurries and a quarterback hit against the Spartans and 2 more hurries against the Terrapins. "I think I'm playing probably the best I have in four years right now," Van Poppel said after Nebraska's Week 4 win over Michigan State . Van Poppel has also been a vocal leader for Nebraska, especially after earning a single-digit jersey last year and being given the option of keeping it this fall. Instead of once again wearing No. 5, he went back to his No. 44, saying he didn't believe he lived up to his own standard of what a player wearing a single digit jersey should be like. “He (Rhule) gave me the option to keep one, but I don’t see it that way. I want the guys who were truly voted to be the single digits, and if I need to go back to a different number, at the end of the day, it’s a number.” As is the policy with the Big Ten Availability Reports, it's not a guarantee that Riley Van Poppel will miss Nebraska's biggest game of the year. The Huskers will release two more before game time. One report will update the status of injured players on Friday night, and another two hours before kickoff. away.headline: Nebraska's lineup is taking shape of exhibition play, but Orme's injury looms
Oregon's Dante Moore, Dylan Raiola, an Injury and a Brock Thomas QB Competition for Nebraska
away.blurb: But at Autzen Stadium, one QB is going to run out for the first offensive snap for the Ducks, and no matter who it is, it'll be a fascinating decision. Oregon's Dante Moore, Dylan Raiola, an Injury and a Brock Thomas QB Competition for Nebraska The Oregon Ducks are home on Saturday night to host the Nebraska Cornhuskers. For those tuned in to these two teams, there are a lot of narratives at play — and many of them stem from the Ducks' QB depth chart of Dante Moore, Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. It's the kind of situation that may or may not get more clarity before kickoff on Saturday. Is Dante Moore Playing This Week? The intrigue starts with Moore, whose playing status for the game against Nebraska seems to remain uncertain. He hasn't played since being concussed against USC on a dirty hit after he slid to the turf. Raiola replaced him in that game, then the Ducks had a bye, and then Raiola started last week. Whether or not Moore will miss another game is a crucial factor one way or the other, but it doesn't seem decided. Is Dylan Raiola Starting This Week? The next factor at play is Raiola, who was pulled midway through Oregon's loss to UCLA. He was just 6-for-19 for 43 yards with two interceptions before head coach Dan Lanning pulled him in the fourth quarter. Lanning told reporters at the start of this week that if Moore can't go on Saturday, that will bring about a QB competition in practice for who starts against the Cornhuskers. Of course, Raiola would love to face Nebraska. That's the school he played at for two years after being the No. 1 quarterback recruit in the country. Then he transferred to Oregon in the offseason, and it seemed he'd just be the backup when the Ducks played the Cornhuskers — but now there's at least a chance he starts. Thomas began the year as Oregon's third quarterback, but he went 11-for-15 for 156 yards and a touchdown in an attempted comeback against UCLA. He's not the high-pedigree recruit of the Ducks' other two quarterbacks, but sometimes productivity gets rewarded. Thomas is actually a cool story, because he's from Eugene and played locally at Sheldon High School. He played in a state title game in high school and also won a 4×100-meter relay state title on the track. A three-star recruit, Thomas picked the hometown team as a third-generation Ducks player — his grandfather Paul Bauge and father Aaron Thomas both played at Oregon, too. home.blurb: Coming out of a bye week with extra time to rest and recover, fans waited for the first injury report for the No. 13 Oregon Ducks' matchup against the No. 21 UCLA Bruins with perhaps more anticipation than usual. While fans will have to wait a little longer to see him in action, Moore's teammates expressed the boost in morale the team gained from seeing him in practice. Lanning addressed having him out there during his Wednesday press conference. "Yeah, I think the biggest thing is just being able to see a smile on his face to get around and be around his teammates and his brothers and do that at a high level, which is fun," Lanning said. "Everybody has a smile on their face getting to see Dante out there with us this week, and it's been fun seeing him compete." "He had an expectation when he stepped out there on the field and performed at a really high level, and everybody had confidence in him because they see him do it a lot in practice," Lanning said. "You get a lot of reps in practice, regardless of where you're sitting." As soon as Moore announced in the offseason that he'd forgo the 2026 NFL Draft and return to Oregon, the outside expectation from many was that the transfer Raiola would back up Moore and become a regular starter in 2027. But with Moore's injury and slow build-up to his return to play keeping him out against the Bruins, Saturday could mark Raiola's starting debut at Oregon. Ducks linebacker Jerry Mixon expressed on Tuesday that Raiola's prior experience and his preparation give the team confidence in him. "He's been ready the whole time, learning from Dante," Mixon said. "Yeah, he's been starting for two years, so he knows what to do when he get out there."
